entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d6 + 4}) Piercing damage plus 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Cold damage, and the target has the {@condition Slowed|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} condition until the end of the troll's next turn. Critical {@h}The target has the {@condition Frozen|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} condition (escape {@dc 16}).

action.name: Slam
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 2d6 + 4}) Bludgeoning damage plus 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Cold damage.

action.name: Freezing Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 16}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Cold damage and has the {@condition Frozen|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} condition (escape {@dc 16}). {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage only.

trait.name: Conditioned Obedience
entries: While the patient can see its creator, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.

action.name: Rusty Surgical Blade
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Slashing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Poison damage.

reaction.name: Protective Impulse
entries: {@actTrigger} The patient's creator is targeted by an attack or spell, and the patient is within 10 feet of it. {@actResponse} The patient switches spaces with its creator and becomes the target instead.

spellcasting.name: Mage Hand
headerEntries: The dragon casts {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB} using Charisma as the spellcasting ability. The hand created by the spell is invisible.

trait.name: Fully Contaminated
entries: The dragon is immune to {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} and has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against contaminated spells. The dragon may cast contaminated spells even though it does not gain {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} levels.

trait.name: Delerium Healing
entries: As an action, the dragon can touch a delerium shard to regain 10 ({@dice 3d6}) {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. Once the dragon has used a delerium shard in this way, the shard can't be used in this manner again for 24 hours.

trait.name: Alien Intellect
entries: The dragon is immune to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, as well as any divination spell that it refuses. Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) checks made to ascertain the dragon's intentions or sincerity have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

trait.name: Haze Aura
entries: A creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of the dragon takes 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Necrotic damage.

action.name: The dragon always takes its turn on Initiative count 20
entries: On its turn, the dragon can use its movement and interaction as normal. However, it does not take an action or {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on its turn unless forced to do so by a spell or other effect. Instead, the dragon takes one of the following {@variantrule Epic Action|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Epic Actions} at the end of each player character's turn:

items.name: Bite
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 10}, reach 10 ft. {@h}17 ({@damage 2d10 + 6}) Force damage, and if the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 18}). While {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, the target has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Contaminated Rend
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 18}, one creature within 5 feet of the dragon. {@actSaveFail} 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Necrotic damage, and the target gains one {@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} level.

items.name: Tail
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 18}, one creature within 20 feet of the dragon. {@actSaveFail} 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Force damage, and if the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

action.name: Octarine Breath {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 18}, each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Necrotic damage plus 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Psychic damage plus 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Radiant damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

action.name: Dimension Hop (1/Round)
entries: The dragon teleports to an unoccupied space it can see within 30 feet.

action.name: Epic Resistance
entries: The dragon chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting them and rolls {@dice 1d20}. On an 11+, the effect ends on it. The dragon can use this action even if it would otherwise be unable to take actions, its actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters its game statistics.

trait.name: Unshakeable Faith (1/Day)
entries: When the zealot would fail a saving throw, it can reroll the save with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. It must use the new roll.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The zealot makes two Greatsword attacks.

action.name: Greatsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5}, reach 5 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d6 + 3}) Slashing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Radiant damage.

bonus.name: For the Flame (1/Day)
entries: Allies of the zealot within 60 feet of it that can hear it gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and saving throws until the start of the zealot's next turn.

trait.name: Blood Frenzy
entries: The vampire has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on melee attack rolls against a creature with the {@status Bloodied|XPHB} condition.

trait.name: Blood Shield
entries: Whenever the vampire damages a creature that has blood, the vampire gains 15 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}.

trait.name: Regeneration
entries: The vampire regains 10 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} and isn't in sunlight or running water. If the vampire takes Radiant damage or damage from holy water, this trait doesn't function at the start of the vampire's next turn.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The vampire can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Vampire Weaknesses
entries: The vampire has the traits described in the "Vampire Weaknesses" sidebar in the Monsters of Drakkenheim.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The vampire makes three attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Bite.

action.name: Claws
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 8}, reach 5 ft. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d4 + 5}) Slashing damage, and if the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape {@dc 21}).

action.name: Bite
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 16}, one creature within 5 feet that is willing or has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, or {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveFail} 15 ({@damage 3d6 + 5}) Necrotic damage. The target's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} Maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken, and the vampire regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to that amount.

bonus.name: Morrigan's Fury (1/Short Rest)
entries: The vampire howls at the moon, gaining {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage except Acid and Radiant damage for 1 minute or until it has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. As part of this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, the vampire moves up to half its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} toward a {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} creature without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB} action.

The grim-faced doctor's jaw tightens as they lower their browand sigh. Suddenly, their face contorts into a wicked, impossiblegrimace, a smile stretched too wide for the muscles on their face.Fiendish light glimmers in their eyes as hornlike bulges rip throughthe flesh of their forehead. Profane runes suddenly blaze upontheir flesh, releasing the smell of burning meat and sulfur. Thebody rises into the air, the muscle spasms barely containing the evilspirit bound within this mortal host. A spiral of flame encircles theapothecary's body as they unleash a horrific scream, speaking in avoice which is not their own. "Now, you will die, mortal."

A Soulbound Host is the physical body of an apothecary who has willingly allowed an extraplanar creature to possess them, trapping the powerful outsider in a mortal form. Powerful yet vulnerable, Soulbound Hosts loathe their creators. They wander the world for the means to reverse the curse of mortality placed upon them and return to their otherworldly domains.

Exorcist and Alienist apothecaries do not primarily study the body, and rarely practice the type of magic and science which leads to mutant horrors and flesh-stitched abominations. They are instead concerned with the supernatural forces of the mind and soul. Many research and contact powerful extraplanar entities, eager to possess mortals as a means of entering the material world. These apothecaries learn how to create Soulbound Hosts as a powerful means to contain and fight back against these dangerous otherworldly foes.

entries.name: Desperate Gambit
entries: A Soulbound Host is usually created under truly desperate circumstances, such as when a heroic apothecary faces a dangerous otherworldly being such as a demon, fey, spirit, or inscrutable entity from the Space Between Worlds. Not only are these planar invaders pernicious foes, many are effectively immortal—often these creatures simply reform when killed outside their native planes. Thus, an apothecary who lacks the ability to defeat the demon on their own, or who wishes to defeat a powerful outsider in a more permanent fashion, may instead decide upon a heroic act of self-sacrifice by turning themselves into a Soulbound Host.

entries.name: Preparing the Trap
entries: Using an array of implanted metals, ingested tinctures, mental preparations, and occult incantations, a skilled apothecary may willingly prepare their body for possession. During the process, the apothecary can weave a unique spiritual trap. It then falls to the apothecary to convince the otherworldly creature to possess them, an act that many outsiders are eager to do. Thus, the canny apothecary preys on the ego of the monster itself.

entries.name: Mortal Curse
entries: When the outsider inhabits the body, the apothecary's soul departs, leaving the extraplanar creature to take their place spiritually. If this mortal form is killed or destroyed, the bound creature does not simply return to their plane of origin. Instead, the spirit departs to the afterworlds like any other mortal soul, losing their accumulated otherworldly power forever. Thus, the Soulbound Host becomes both a prison and a death sentence for the other wielding being tricked into the apothecary's body.

entries.name: Rogue Hosts
entries: Unfortunately, this act of self-sacrifice is not without its imperfections. The apothecary's body is filled with otherworldly essence, and while the creature's power is greatly diminished, they often remain extremely dangerous—allies of the departed apothecary may still find it challenging to slay the Soulbound Host. Many escape, wandering the world with stolen lives and even assuming the identity of their host while they search for the means to escape their now mortal form. All bound outsiders are painfully aware of their new mortality, frustrated that returning to their planes of origin is not a simple matter of destroying their flesh-cage or switching their essence into a different host, one which lacks the binding wards placed by the apothecary.

entries.name: Price of Freedom
entries: Trapped outsiders can win their freedom by calling back the soul of the apothecary who trapped them, and resurrecting them into their body. This is a thing many outsiders are loathe to do out of fiendish ego, since it puts the original soul in a bargaining position. In this way, the apothecary can force the spirit to accept a bargain which requires them to remain in their own worlds for at least the duration of the apothecary's lifetime.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Religion|XPHB}, {@skill Medicine|XPHB}, or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to Study a Soulbound Host, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (10+) Possessed Body
entries: You know the Soulbound Host's type and damage {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}.

entries.name: (15+) Extraplanar Magic
entries: Depending on the type of spirit, you learn either the Hellfire Chain, Illusory Assault, or Psychic Barrage actions, as well as the Spellcasting trait of the host.

entries.name: (20+) Cursed Fate
entries: You recognize its desperation caused by its spirit-bound mortality and its Reactions.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: A Soulbound Host is a careful combatant. Though powerful, the last thing they want is to be killed in their mortal form. If they are seriously injured, they often attempt to bargain, offering power and knowledge to assailants who spare them.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Fiend, Fey, or Aberrant.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Claws.

entries.name: Hair:
entries: Hair.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Skin.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Fiendish, Fey, or Aberrant Dust.

items.name: Academy Apprentice

entries: Dressed in simple purple robes with the symbol of the Amethyst Academy upon their left breast, the apprentice carries a spellbook fastened to their belt, and a simple satchel of alchemical ingredients.

These mages-in-training have completed enough study to cast level 1 arcane spells. The Amethyst Academy often assigns apprentices to higher-ranked mages, where they assist with research, experimentation, and fieldwork. One or more apprentices often accompany a Master Mage.

items.name: Academy Grandmaster

entries: The Academy Grandmaster wears a purple and gold jacket and trousers, with an Academy's insignia broach on their lapel and glimmering rings on each finger. They carry an ornate gold and black staff topped with a glimmering {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystal}. Their eyes crackle with energy, harnessing the raw power around them.

These are powerful spellcasters who can cast level 9 spells. They lead the Amethyst Academy's most important projects and can access almost every resource available within. Only a handful exist: beyond the eight members of the Academy Directorate, there are no more than twenty alive today. In the rare event of a vacancy, the Master Mages may nominate Grandmasters for consideration. Since the Directorate must unanimously choose one to join them, openings can take decades to fill.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Their first action is to cast {@spell Time Stop|XPHB}, followed by {@spell Wall of Force} to trap as many foes as possible. Those who aren't entrapped are blasted with {@spell Prismatic Spray}, {@spell Chain Lightning}, and {@spell Fireball}.
They flee using {@spell Teleport} when {@status Bloodied|XPHB}.

items.name: Academy Mage

entries: Dressed in a purple long jacket with gold trim, dark trousers and simple black boots, the mage carries a wand in one hand and a book in the other, with the symbol of the Amethyst Academy emblazoned upon the back of their jacket in gold.

These rank-and-file members of the Amethyst Academy can cast spells of up to level 3 or 4. Apprentices qualify for this rank when they can cast at least level 2 spells. Most Academy mages conduct research or craft magic items for the Amethyst Academy, and a handful join survey teams exploring ancient sites or the ruins of Drakkenheim. Others are assigned as court mages for low-ranking nobility. The majority of Academy mages never attain a higher rank than this one.

items.name: Academy Outcast

entries: Dressed in a simple brown trench coat, with black trousers and boots and a simple white shirt, the Academy Outcast sports a pair of welding goggles upon their unkempt hair. With a sly expression upon their face, they hold their wands at the ready.

Not all mageborn are cut out for the rules, regulations, and intense study and practice required by the Amethyst Academy, and some do not make it through their schooling. An outcast may still be under the guidance of the Academy, performing field work or odd jobs that require a more hands-on approach. Oftentimes these outcasts dabble in dangerous magics, and have far less caution, and far too much confidence for the Academy's liking
One of the strongest was an academy outcast. For those who are expelled, what's the worst that can happen?

items.name: Adult Delerium Dragon
entries: A fully mature Delerium Dragon establishes its own domain within the Space Between Worlds, finding a place suitable to its temperament. There it seeks to understand itself and the world around it.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Aberration.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts, Glands, Flesh.

entries.name: Bones:
entries: Skull, Spine, Ribs.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Claws, Teeth.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Scales, Webbed Membrane.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Aberrant Dust.

entries.name: Delerium
entries: In addition, characters can collect {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals} from its body: an adult has {@dice 2d6} crystals.

monsterFluff.name: Agog

entries: This horrific thing has no shape or body resembling anything from the Mortal World. It roughly resembles a tree stump with four root-like legs each ending in a misshapen hoof. It has a wet, mottled, bark-like hide, and sprouting from the side of it like branches are knobbly arms ending in sharp claws. The top of its body is a gaping, tooth-filled mouth. It is shoveling chunks of horse-flesh into itself, and giggling as it swallows the ripped flesh. Whatever passes for arms, on the inside of the palm are yellow eyes.

The Agog resembles what mortals might comprehend as a tree stump, and when the creature is motionless, it may even be passed by. However, when it springs to life its true form is something wholly bizarre. These creatures waddle along desert landscapes in the Space Between Worlds, or rest in the muck surrounding the screaming heads. They feed on corpses and have a seemingly endless appetite and a need to satiate it.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine an Agog, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (5+) Climbing Aberration
entries: You know the creature's type, and movement speeds.

entries.name: (10+) Attack the Fallen
entries: You are aware of the creature's Gobble Bonus Action.

entries.name: (15+) Dim but Sturdy
entries: You recognize the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Agog barrels towards its enemies, flailing its arms towards them and attempting to grab them and toss them to the ground. If it knocks a creature down, it will immediately begin attempting to devour them.

entries.name: Animus:
entries: Aberration.

entries.name: Fluid:
entries: Contaminated Ichor, Sap.

entries.name: Organs:
entries: Guts.

entries.name: Natural Weapons:
entries: Claws, Teeth.

entries.name: Hide:
entries: Bark.

entries.name: Dust:
entries: Aberrant Dust.
I don't know if I want these guys poking around in my head! That's where I keep my thoughts!

Hovering inches from the ground, lab coat billowing in an unknown breeze that seems to swirl around the figure, the Alienist mutters under their breath, eyes glowing white as they pull on the threads of your mind. You feel the imminent threat of your psyche shattering to this apothecary's will with little more than a flick of their wrist.

An Alienist seeks to master the mysteries of the mind. Having devoted years to studying the inner workings of the brain to unlock its latent potential, an Alienist is able to bend reality, read thoughts, and manipulate the thoughts of others. They tap into unfathomable realities and shift the world to their will using the psychic energies they call upon from eldritch lore and arcane knowledge.

entries.name: Alienist Minions
entries: Alienists keep several experiments of their own on hand. They have been known to keep {@creature Wretched Patient|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Wretched Patients}, their minds melted by the Alienist's inhuman experimentation, turning them into obedient and loyal servants. {@creature Disembodied Psyche|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Disembodied Psyches} and {@creature Cerebrograft|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Cerebrografts} are a few of their higher-end creations, having removed the brain of a creature and given it a unique and bespoke form of sentience, these creatures serve as guards to an Alienist's work, or minions capable of complex thought and aid.

items: {@b Personality Trait:} I can't help but analyze every person who comes before me. I want to know what they think, and why they are the way they are.
{@b Bond:} I study the mind for scientific advancement. How easily this muscle can be manipulated, altered, and used in unforeseen ways is fascinating research that must be explored.
{@b Ideal:} I am the only one capable of this level of advanced mental research, someone else would have gotten it wrong
{@b Flaw:} My unbound intellect means that I can never be fooled, tricked, or manipulated, and thus I can never be outsmarted, to think I could is laughable.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Medicine|XPHB} or {@skill Arcana|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to {@action study|XPHB} an Alienist, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (10+) Mental Master
entries: You are aware of the Alienist's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} as well as its Unmatched Intellect trait.

entries.name: (15+) Mind Control
entries: You know of its Mass Manipulation action.

entries.name: (20+) Brilliant but Vulnerable
entries: You learn its AC, as well as its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Wretched Patients are simple minions. They defend themselves and reluctantly fight at the command of their creator. If their creator dies, Wretched Patients flee or cower.
His mouth isn't moving but I can hear everything he's saying, I guess it's time to silence the voices.

monsterFluff.name: Allopine

entries: This creature has a gaunt and misshapen form, with the scaled body, tail, and head of an alligator, bony spikes covering its body like a porcupine, batlike wings, and long, spindly limbs.

The Allopine is a creature that defies logic, seemingly a shifting and confused array of various animals—its disjointed and bizarre arrangements make them a puzzle to look at. Flying through the Space Between Worlds, the creatures travel in swarms occupying the dark caverns and ruins found throughout the non-places. When making their way into the Mortal World, they will find old barns or caves to hide in.

entries.name: Study the Foe

entries.name: Combat Tactics

monsterFluff.name: Amalgamation

entries: Before the throne is a gibbering amalgamation of fleshy tumors, rotting bones, and rancid layers of bloated fat suspended between the ceiling and floor by stalky strands of gnarled tissue. A palpable aura of contamination emanates from the beast. The mass is covered in bursting sores and shuddering mucus nodule that weep bile and delerium sludge. The creature mutters in alien tongues from six yawning mouths, piping and sputtering in discordant musical tones, and lazily shifting eyes of massive size open and close throughout its bulk. Thick trunk-like tentacles reach out from its hideous stinking form to squirm and writhe around the chamber. Several appendages are wrapped around pulsing human organs: lungs, liver, kidney, a heart, a brain, and dangling amongst them is the jeweled Crown of Westemär.
Dwelling within the throne room of Castle Drakken is the Amalgamation, the result of a cascading catastrophe of contamination and mutation.

When the meteor struck, several magical occurrences happened almost instantaneously throughout the city. The Fracturing of the Inscrutable Tower triggered haywire {@table Arcane Anomalies|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Arcane Anomaly} through the city, while the impact of the meteor sent a shockwave of magical devastation that shattered glass, blew through stone and wood, and reduced most living creatures to ash. Others caught in the blast were instantly transformed into monsters, and buildings and streets were shifted into sentient growths and misshapen horrors.

Castle Drakken was an epicenter of magical wards, protective spells, divination, and all manner of inherently magical trinkets and artifacts. The throne room where King Ulrich sat housed several of the most powerful magical relics in Westemär. The Crown of Westemär being the most prominent, although King Ulrich himself held a magical scepter, wore four magical rings, and a possessed a protective amulet. Furthermore, the large circular stained glass window behind the throne was imbued with magic that allowed it to change colors and depict different images throughout the seasons.

Naturally, when the rippling wave of arcane destruction blasted through the throne room, it fractured the abundant magical energies within the room, immediately opening a rift to the Space Between Worlds (see chapter 8) and amalgamating all the king's men into a massive mound of rippling fatty flesh. King Ulrich tried to escape but the magical mayhem fused him to his throne. As the King melted, he was absorbed by the expanding flesh, his face coming to rest as a disfigured grimace placed in the center of the horrible Amalgamation.

The creature continued to grow as the years passed, and those who went searching for the lost king would soon become one with the Amalgamation as well. Tendrils of strange flesh now spread like a web of sinew and skin across the throne room while pulsing contamination ripples out of the grotesque mass. A massive maw spans the length of the creature with various human bones posing as jagged and sharp teeth. Its tongue is a writhing mass of intestines and gore. No longer can any semblance of those lost to the Amalgamation be found. The king's face still prominently sits above the creature's massive maw, a mocking display of the fragility of the empires of a world not ready to face horrors beyond their comprehension.

The Amalgamation has a multidimensional form that straddles the Material Plane and the Space Between Worlds. Its mere presence acts as an anchor for the dimensional rift that pulls more and more contamination into Drakkenheim.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters who have one or more mutations, or who are afflicted with any form of madness gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they {@action Study|XPHB} the Amalgamation, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (20+) Multidimensional
entries: You recognize its {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, and its Rejuvenation, Malignancy, and Immutable Form traits.

entries.name: (25+) Insatiable Hunger
entries: You know of the creature's Bite attack, as well as its Mind-Breaking Whispers ability.

entries.name: (30+) Beyond Comprehension
entries: You are aware of its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Amalgamation is a formidable foe capable of grappling multiple targets and eating them or throwing them around the battlefield. It constantly summons {@creature Pyknic Maunder|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Pyknic Maunders} as additional support while it uses Mind-Breaking Whispers to shatter the minds of its greatest threats.
The Amalgamation does not fear any mortal creature, believing itself indestructible to mortal means. It does not flee or cower.

entries.name: Amethyst Academy
entries: The wizards of the Amethyst Academy perform all sorts of arcane tasks throughout the nations. They study ancient ruins, maintain their magical strongholds, accompany nobles on errands, or participate as members of their council. These mages are well known throughout the continent and are identifiable by their purple-robes and academy rings.

entries.name: Academy Combat Tactics
entries: Broadly speaking, Amethyst Academy mages eschew combat, valuing their own lives too highly to take such risks. They view themselves as researchers, craftspeople, and scholars, not war mages—few bother learning damaging spells beyond simple cantrips, instead focusing on practical magic for their academic and industrial pursuits. Nevertheless, they know that magic is still a dangerous vocation, and ready themselves to flee perilous situations with {@spell Invisibility|XPHB} spells or teleportation magic.

When violent confrontation seem inevitable, Amethyst Academy agents often hire mercenaries or adventurers, or dispatch summoned creatures in their stead. Nevertheless, there are bold explorers who take to field research and prepare themselves for dangerous expeditions—particularly, those who personnally study the ruins of Drakkenheim. They often utilize constructs such as Shield Guardians or summoned elementals bound to service with {@spell Planar Binding}. Mages usually begin combat with defensive or control spells as befits the situation, such as taking to the air with {@spell Fly} or subduing foes with {@spell Slow}. Only once they are certain the situation is under control will they use their signature Prismatic Blasts or area-of-effect spells like {@spell Fireball} and {@spell Lightning Bolt}. These mages almost always flee once they've become {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, viewing a temporary setback or mission failure as a preferable outcome over their deaths.

items.name: Ancient Delerium Dragon
entries: Perhaps older than the cosmos itself, Ancient Delerium Dragons possess knowledge and memories of worlds and eons which have past, many more which never were, and countless which cannot be. Their very presence warps the world around them according to their whims.

monsterFluff.name: Animated Delerium Sludge

entries: A mound of iridescently streaked black muck lumbers through the ruins, splashing with each ponderous step. The sludge reshapes into a towering, almost human-like form, with slimy arms and thick unsteady legs. A head bubbles atop its viscous body revealing a slime drooling maw and two hollows for eyes. Yet, it carries a strangely mirthful expression, as if finding joy in its grotesque existence. The mound emits a gravelly roar, full of sinister glee, and barrels towards you, undeterred by the debris in its way.
These Contaminated Water Elementals are often found in the cisterns, sewers, and other aquatic locations of Drakkenheim.

entries.name: Study the Foe

entries.name: (15+) Contamination by Contact
entries: You are aware of its Contaminated Touch and Engulf actions.

entries.name: (20+) Easy to Outwit
entries: You know the elemental's mental ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Animated Delerium Sludge often lies dormant in bodies of water before attempting to Engulf an unsuspecting creature. If reduced to less than 20 Hit Points, it attempts to slip back into the nearby sludge and Hide, hoping to be left alone.

monsterFluff.name: Anomollusk

entries: A colossal snail as wide as a city street with a shell the size of a small house glides slowly into view. Its shell has a kaleidoscopic fractal shimmer, projecting hues of unknown colors that swirl in incomprehensible patterns. As it moves, its shell seems to refract light in ways that seem nonsensical or wrong. You must strain your eyes to look at it wriggle towards you. Its bulbous head ends in two long antennae each holding a small octarine eye. Slimy mucus drips off its flesh, leaving sizzling trails and corroding anything it touches.

When a simple snail latches onto a delerium shard, there is a slight chance it fuses with its shell. These humble creatures can grow to massive proportions if they survive the contamination. Over time, the shells merge with more delerium, mutating the snails into chaotic conduits for erratic magic called an Anomollusk.

Its defensive crystalline shells can also absorb arcane energy. This adaptation disrupts nearby magic, rendering spells and magical weapons unreliable. Attacking an Anomollusk with magic is dangerous, causing wild magic flares and {@table Arcane Anomalies|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Arcane Anomaly}, giving the creature its name. Driven to consume contaminated flora, Anomollusks inadvertently collect magical energy, making them especially valuable for creating magic items.

Anomollusks are predominantly found in areas like Queen's Park Garden, where the flora is richly imbued with magic. Though sometimes seen in the city's outskirts, they prefer heavily contaminated areas such as around the Crater's Edge. These creatures absorb and occasionally release magical energy from the environment, unleashing sporadic bursts of chaotic magic in the landscape.

In their wake, Anomollusks leave trails of acidic decay—ichors far too toxic even for their bodies to contain for long. Moving with lackadaisical whimsy, they etch eerie patterns into stone and metal, occasionally resembling arcane runes when observed from above. If there is any meaning or purpose behind these markings, none can say for certain.

entries.name: Study the Foe

entries.name: (15+) Dangerous Slime

entries.name: (20+) Slow and Simple Minded

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Drawn to magic, Anomollusk's view spellcasters and those equipped with magic items as delicious morsels. It attacks by first using its Creep action before it tries to Slobber on them. If threatened, it tries to cover the enemy and its territory in acidic slime. If reduced to less than half Hit Points, it attempts to flee.

A perfect physical form of humanity stands before you, its flawlessly formed and muscle-bound flesh is tinted in a golden hue while its veins bulge and glow with octarine light. Their eyes emit cascades of light and their voice is a booming chorus. As swirls of fire, ice, and electricity crackle around them, they pulse with unbound energy.

entries.name: Perfect Transmogrification
entries: Amongst {@creature Mutagenist|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Mutagenists}, the quest for genetic perfection can become an all-consuming obsession. Those who seek to achieve this so-called superior state refer to it as the "Apex" and describe the transformation as creating the ultimate humanoid specimen.

Through years of study and trials, Mutagenists have perfected their Transmogrifying Elixir to harness the ultimate power of mortal potential. This formula allows them to amplify their natural capabilities to the peak physical form while maintaining their unbound intellect. There is no telling how many long years a Mutagenist has spent in their lab, and how many unwilling test subjects had to suffer the fates of their imperfect formulae before they arrived at the ultimate conclusion of their research. This is the pinnacle of their scientific study, the perfected Transmogrifying Elixir: the Apex Formula.

entries.name: Permanent Transformation
entries: The process renders the Mutagenist permanently altered. Energy courses through their veins, their strength and agility extended to the very limits of human capabilities. Their form is able to shift and adapt to incoming threats, and they are able to perceive events around them with great precision. Their mind, although it remains intellectually intact by the process, is inherently and irrevocably shattered. No Mutagenist who takes the Apex Formula could ever perceive or admit to the fracturing of their mind. Regardless of their vast intelligence, a sickening madness takes hold of their psyche; one that plunges the apothecary-turned-Apex creature into a hostile, madness-filled rage. They still hold onto the threads of their vast scientific mind, using that as a justification for their actions, unaware of the deranged mental state they now reside within.

entries.name: The Folly of Perfection
entries: Even Mutagenists who achieve the Apex state have a gnawing question in the back of their minds: is it truly enough? Could they become even more? Their seemingly perfect form is not without subtle flaws, broken psyche, and weaknesses. Many Mutagenists can never truly be satisfied with their results, and even the Apex Formula can never fulfill the unattainable desire for absolute perfection. It is this obsession that has led many Mutagenists to lunacy in the face of their achievements. For even an Apex may spend eternity bound to their workshop, kidnapping unwilling subjects to continue to test and experiment, seeking a perfection that will never truly be achieved.

entries.name: Roleplaying Traits
entries: The following traits can be used to inspire roleplaying the Cacophonous Chimera:

items: {@b Personality Trait:} I am humanity perfected! All beings are beneath me, for I am the apex of physical existence. All should cower in my glory
{@b Bond:} Science has granted us this gift! This research is the most valuable scientific discovery in the world and must be protected!
{@b Ideal:} Do not try and stop me, for I am offering perfection to all of humanity. Can't you see? The Apex Form will cure the world of all sickness, all flaws, all weakness!
{@b Flaw:} There cannot be a weakness in my design. If there is, I will solve it — I just need more time!

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Medicine|XPHB}, {@skill Survival|XPHB}, or {@skill Arcana|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} the Apex. , learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (15+) Adapts to Threats
entries: You recognize the Apex's Rapid Adaptation {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and Regeneration trait.

entries.name: (20+) Harness the Elements
entries: You are aware of its {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} attacks.

entries.name: (25+) Perfect Form but Fragile Mind
entries: You know the Apex's weakness to Necrotic and Psychic damage.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Apex will often be accompanied by several abominations of its own creation. Lab assistants, failed experiments, and {@creature Wretched Patient|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Wretched Patients} are often by its side.

An Apex begins combat by unleashing one of its {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} attacks. It quickly analyzes the battlefield, looking for the most optimal use of its energy. It observes the arrangement of its enemies and decides if it is best to use its lightning, fire, or cold attack based on what will deliver the most damage to the most targets.
It then uses its speed to move close to a target to smash it with its Slam attacks. The Apex prefers to target Frozen enemies with its Slams.

The Apex is unwilling to see its own flaws, but it is not stupid. If reduced below 60 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it unleashes a final attack and attempts to distance itself from its enemies, hoping to escape and recuperate.

monsterFluff.name: Arcane Wraith

entries: Tattered purple robes hang off the ethereal skeleton drifting silently through the air. Its rune-inscribed skull menacingly chants arcane words as points of octarine light flare from the dark holes of its eyes. Ghostly tendrils flicker and five Academy rings jangle as it raises a skeletal hand, enacting the arcane gestures of its first spell.

An Arcane Wraith is the disembodied, corrupt, undead spirit of an arcane spellcaster who perished violently in Drakkenheim. Delerium affects people with magical skill in unpredictable ways. In their death throes, those with mageborn blood may transform into vile undead, eternally bound to the Haze while retaining a portion of their arcane power twisted into malevolent, shadowy forms. Arcane Wraiths relentlessly hunger for both magical essence and life force. They are particularly aggressive towards living spellcasters, but readily attack anyone carrying magic items, spell components, or {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals}.

These wraiths are most frequently seen near highly magical areas, like the Inscrutable Tower, however, they have been spotted elsewhere in the Inner City, and rarely, outside the city walls. Places like potion shops and a mage's former residence are also common haunts for an Arcane Wraith.

Left alone, these spirits ponderously study arcane phenomena, often drawing paradoxical conclusions. They collect scrolls, and spellbooks while scribbling rambling notes. Occasionally, their mad research may uncover a genuine revelation, but discerning discovery from delusion amidst their tattered scrawlings is difficult. A careful approach may allow one to converse with these undead. However, their speech is a convoluted mixture of half-remembered incantations, loquacious postulations, and incoherent babbling. They quickly grow frustrated when interlocutors fail to grasp the brilliance of their work.

entries.name: (10+) Spellcaster's Spirit
entries: You are aware of its Comet Shards and Nightmare Pattern actions.

entries.name: (15+) Unstable Intellect
entries: You recognize the monster's strongest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Arcane Wraiths take advantage of their Incorporeal Movement, gliding through walls and small openings, before blasting targets with Comet Shards from above. They use Nightmare Pattern to control foes and focus attacks on those unaffected by the illusion. Occasionally, they collaborate with other undead, such as Haze Husks and Haze Wights, commanding them like apprentices or minions.

items.name: Ascendant Vladimir von Drakken

entries: Covered in the gore exploded from his regal form, Vladimir von Drakken has become a hulking monstrosity. Now twelve feet tall, his upper frame is hunched over, and his arms support him like a gorilla. Spiked bones and frilled f ins emerge from his arms and his clawed hands are large enough to crush skulls. Bladed scythes and spikes sprout from great batlike wings. The remains of his armor and cloak hang over his swelling new form. Bony protrusions jut from his head like a demonic crown. His once-imperial countenance is gone, replaced by a beastly face, a cross between wolf, bat, and dragon. Trickling blood and sweat, he breathes heavily between grunts, growls, and roars, barely uttering a sentence without howling.
In his Ascendant form, Vladimir von Drakken is truly a monster. Once he ascends to this form, he savagely attacks anyone he sees, including his own underlings.

monsterFluff.name: Beetle Knight

entries: Two insectoid legs hold up the beetle-like creature, rhythmically clacking as it skitters about. Two clawed arms scrabble beneath blade-like limbs as gnashing mandibles chitter under its beady eyes. A massive pincer-like horn protrudes from its helmet-shaped head and a tough blueish-silver shell protects delicate wings hidden beneath.

Beetle Knights represent the mutations found within even the smallest creatures in the aftermath of the meteor's strike. Insects that once crawled up from the soil, out of wall cracks, or from between floor boards have been transformed by contact with delerium and exposure to the Haze. Many have grown monstrously, to humanoid size or even larger.

Beetle Knight shells are thick enough to protect them from most attacks. Their name comes from the way their shells have mutated to resemble plate armor, while scything hands and a massive horn look like a pair of blades and an ornate helm. At a glance, these creatures resemble an armored knight ready for battle.

Beetle Knights commonly hide within the ruins and sewers of Drakkenheim, feeding on Deep Dregs and other smaller creatures. Occasionally, at night, or after heavy rains, Beetle Knights emerge in large numbers, to surprise and overwhelm the unprepared.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to study a Beetle Knight, revealing the following based on the result:

entries: You identify its condition {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (10+) Watch Out for that Horn!
entries: You recognize its Fling {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, and Pincer Horn action.

entries.name: (15+) Slow and Unintelligent
entries: You know its strongest and weakest saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Beetle Knight is surprisingly agile, rarely standing still in battle. They charge during the first round, flinging enemies aside or attempting to grapple. If possible, they back up to charge again but will otherwise defend with their arm blades. They attempt to flee losing battles where their {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} fall below half their maximum.

monsterFluff.name: Belfray

entries: A shrill screech pierces the air as a large, misshapen bat swoops overhead. Its outstretched wings resemble elongated human arms, with flesh pulled taut to its deformed body. Rows of hooked fangs fill its maw below bulging, red eyes and a sniveling snout.

Once a common sight, bats in Drakkenheim have swelled in both number and form. Many are now as large as dogs with wingspans stretching almost six feet. Insects no longer satisfy their thirst for blood and they crave the taste of flesh.
Belfrays are nocturnal and seldom encountered during the day. Even within the Haze, they prefer the nightly octarine glow to the strange hazy days.

When night falls, Belfrays gather atop old towers and flutter through the streets. They can be found hanging from old lamp posts and in the rafters of ruined houses, waiting to swoop down upon passing creatures. They are most often found in the city's highest locations such as {@i Castle Drakken}, the Clock Tower, the Inscrutable Tower, and some of the city's larger buildings.

Belfrays mostly feast on Ratlings, but many victims have been surprised by these creatures swarming from the darkness. One should always be wary of damp and dark spaces where a handful of Belfrays could lurk. Disturbing them might be your last mistake.

entries.name: (10+) Flying Blood-Drinker
entries: You recognize its Flyby and Keen Hearing features, and Enfeebling Bite attack.

entries.name: (15+) Weak Mind
entries: You know the Belfray's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Belfray attempts to strike with a Sonic Blast from the shadows before engaging. Once a target is weakened, it swoops in with its claws. When damaged, Belfrays Bite, feeding on the blood of their victims to regain strength. It uses movement to stay away from threats, diving to attack before flying to a safe distance. If reduced below half of its maximum Hit Points, it attempts to fly away.

monsterFluff.name: Big Linda

entries: The ground shudders beneath the approach of a monstrosity: a pale, green-white, bipedal reptile. A huge mouth dominates its skull-like face, as acidic saliva drips between rows of razor-sharp teeth. Spines run down its back and tail, and its great body is supported by two trunk-like legs, though its feeble forearms appear nearly useless. It roars a sound like rent metal as it charges forward to devour you.

Hidden beneath the ruins of Drakkenheim, the enigmatic {@b Queen of Thieves} has a vast arena where the ambitious battle for a chance to win her favor. Those who climb its ranks must ultimately face the Queen's favorite pet: a monstrous reptilian creature affectionately nicknamed "Big Linda." Should any survive a minute in the pit—or manage to slay the beast—the Queen of Thieves promises anything within her power to grant. Of course, no one has yet claimed this prize.

Pit fighters are often puzzled by the Queen's calm smirk when they believe they can gain her favor. Few realize that each victory brings them ever closer to a tragic end in Big Linda's jaws while a crowd of thieves cheers on their gruesome deaths.

Big Linda was first spotted in the ruins near King's Gate hunting trolls. No creature like her has been seen, and it remains unclear how the Queen captured the beast. It's thought that she herself played a role, since no one hired for the mission is still alive. Even the crew she paid to deliver the caged beast met their deaths at the hands of a Hooded Lanterns patrol shortly thereafter.

It remains a mystery what creature transformed to become Big Linda, perhaps a mutated bird, or an overgrown gecko. The only creature remotely resembling it is the old dinosaur skeleton in the Drakkenheim museum, but even then, the many differences bring up a slew of questions as to its origin.

Although the Queen keeps Big Linda well-fed and securely contained, she is aware the monstrosity is barely under her control. Maintaining the beast's feeding schedule of fresh "challengers" is difficult and few handlers last more than a week before being gobbled up. The position is seen as a death sentence rather than any position of prestige amongst the Queen's Men.

entries: Big Linda sends Acid Spew against groups of opponents. She then tries to optimize her Bite and Tail attacks by placing herself within her enemies. She is hesitant to leave the Deep Haze but is also not smart enough to resist chasing those who antagonizing her. She rarely flees unless severely wounded, wherein she will seek the safety of the Deep Haze to recover.

monsterFluff.name: Bigger Linda

entries: Thundering through the streets of Drakkenheim with a crash, the infamous pet of the Queen of Thieves has mutated and enlarged to unfathomable proportions. The Haze swirls around it, and octarine energy pulses in its sunken eye sockets. The broken hafts of weapons and old arrows are embedded into its scales, stuck deeply between its regenerated flesh. Its spined back is illuminated by webs of glowing octarine veins; its wide snout is filled with jagged teeth. As it opens its maw wide, the building contaminated energy at the back of its throat begins to glow.

If {@creature Big Linda|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} ever escapes the confines of the {@creature Queen of Thieves|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, the beast will no doubt return to the ruins of Drakkenheim and immediately seek out new hunting grounds. However, Big Linda's containment has stunted her true growth potential. Once freed, the longer Big Linda spends directly exposed to the energies the Haze, the more she grows. As she grows, new mutations begin to form, further amplifying her ferocity, predatory senses, and resilience. If left unchecked, Big Linda might become the apex predator of Drakkenheim—Bigger Linda.

items.name: Blackjack Mel

entries: A short and scrawny man in his late thirties stands before you with a funny-looking but clean-shaven mug and greasy slickedback hair. He wears a black padded jacket and buckled slacks that appear distinguished at first glance but are actually quite shabby and worn.

Blackjack Mel is the Queen of Thieves most trusted advisor. That is to say that she doesn't trust him at all, but knows that he is afraid of her, and will do her bidding as long as she pays him more than others. She pays in protection and a good position. No one is more manipulated by the Queen of Thieves' than Blackjack Mel, who handles much of her communications and business deals with the local gangs.

entries.name: Personality Trait
entries: I can always make a deal with the right angle, I just gotta pitch it the right way. I don't give up when the mark doesn't take the bait, just try something new!

entries.name: Ideal
entries: We're all in this for ourselves. You scratch my back, I'll scratch yours.

entries.name: Bond
entries: Listen, I got some close connections with some powerful people. You wanna meet the Queen of Thieves? Stick with me. We'll go places together. Just uh, watch out you don't piss anyone off, okay?

entries.name: Flaw
entries: I'm a compulsive liar, so what? Yeah, sometimes even
I get confused by my own lies, but the truth can always do with a little exaggeration, it makes life more interesting

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Blackjack Mel is a coward, a swindler, and a thief. He is often surrounded by Thugs and Assassins who protect him; Mel rarely draws a blade. His overconfidence relies on his company, and he will often only take a stab at someone if they are held down.

Mel's first line of defense is his mouth. He will double-cross, backstab, swindle, and con even his allies to ensure his own survival. He knows a lot of information about a lot of things and will use his well of secrets to bargain for his safety. He is also clever and will usually only divulge half of a fact to save his life, ensuring the other half will be granted once his safety is ensured. He knows very well that information is what keeps him alive, and he isn't about to use up that usefulness.
Mel flees without question at any opportunity if he feels threatened, and often keeps a {@item Potion of Invisibility|XDMG} on his person for just such instances.
All bets are off when you're dealing with this thug. He's got info on anything for a price or a threat.

monsterFluff.name: Bloated Dreg

entries: A gurgling moan emerges from the dark as the slopping footsteps of a bloated form emerges. Its rippling, sagging flesh is wet and dripping. Its rotund face and soggy skin are covered in boils, blisters, and leaking sores. Wet, acidic saliva dribbles down its chin, leaving trails of burned flesh. The Dreg's one arm is a mass of writhing slick tentacles. As its mouth opens, a low gurgling sound slowly builds.

People who are submerged in contaminated water often become Bloated Dregs. These half-drowned unfortunates are found near bodies of water throughout the city, such as the sewers or near the Drann River. They have absorbed so much contaminated water into themselves that it festers and mixes with their stomach acids, producing a corrosive bile that they hurl towards their foes. Often a Bloated Dreg will only leave the water for a few hours before finding another puddle of sludge or a contaminated pool to rest in.

entries.name: (15+) Mockery of Humanity

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Bloated Dreg shuffles aimlessly through Drakkenheim, stopping to rest in places where contaminated water has built up, or in pools of delerium sludge. It produces large amounts of acidic bile in its guts that it expels when threatened. A Bloated Dreg will retreat to its watery home when threatened, trying to hide amongst the contaminated liquids.

monsterFluff.name: Bloated Hive

entries: Dripping with sweet smelling pus and mucus, the creature shuffles about on spindly limbs like a gangly ape. It has long gnarled fingers and an emaciated whip-cord thin frame. Where there should be a head there is instead a mass of pulsing flesh covered in gaping pores that extend down its neck and across its shoulders. Its body writhes with thousands of bugs crawling beneath its skin and swarming around its head. They burrow in and out of open wounds and sores and buzz in and out of its pores. It smells faintly of honey and sweat, and gurgles painfully amidst the chorus of buzzing and clicking of insects, as if the thing is painfully aware of its wretched state.

The Bloated Hive is a product of contamination that seems to have turned people into walking hives of insects. Some suspect the honey farms on the outskirts may have been the main source of these strange mutations, causing the apiarists and their hives to warp together, fusing into a grotesque and tortured creature. Their upper torso and head are now a writhing mass of open pores like a beehive, with bugs swarming in and out. They lumber around the ruins looking for nesting places where their hive can thrive. Many Bloated Hives operate alone, but sometimes a much more horrifying event occurs, where a single colony begins to occupy multiple Bloated Hives, forming a horrifying network.

The Bloated Hive tends to hide itself in the dark corners of ruins, often seeking the most damp and warm locations in the city. Many hives have been found along the Drann River within the Inner City, a large group of them living under Champion's Bridge, and even more in the sewers, Queen's Park Garden, and a sparse few in the woods to the north of Drakkenheim. Whenever traversing into dark and damp areas in the city, be on the lookout for an increase in insect activity and the sound of buzzing.

A Bloated Hive cannot speak, and acts on the whims of its occupants more so than its own free thought. Its mind is now a broken thing, connected inherently to the hive mind of a swarm of insects, but within that is a tortured human struggling for sentience. Some Bloated Hives have been known to respond to kind words, trinkets of their former selves, or music they recognize. Though these moments of subtle sentience are fleeting, as the hive reacts quickly to the feeling of an unwanted psyche struggling for dominance within the hive mind and could trigger a frenzied tantrum if not handled delicately.

entries.name: Study the Foe

entries.name: (5+) Sightless Awareness
entries: You know the creature's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} and senses.

entries.name: (10+) Endless Insects!
entries: You are aware of the creature's Spawn Swarm action and Disrupt the Hive trait.

entries.name: (15+) Frail
entries: You recognize the Bloated Hive's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Bloated Hive is usually a solitary creature that spends its time cowering in dark corners living out its cursed life as nothing more than a conduit for its colony. In combat, they focus entirely on keeping their distance from threats and spawning swarms of insects to defend themselves. If cornered, the Bloated Hive uses its Claws and Distracting Swarm before moving back into the shadows and attempting to escape and find a new nest.

Larger packs of Bloated Hives are much braver and more violent, and actively hunt and pursue targets until their numbers are less than their prey. Places where large colonies gather are dangerous. The Bloated Hives work in unison to protect their nests. Only if they become outnumbered do they flee.

items.name: Blood Leech
entries: Although the practice of draining a patient's blood to draw out illness and disease is long discredited, many apothecaries understand the value of transfusing blood during surgical procedures. However, storing the blood long term can be a problem. Apothecaries have solved by modifying normal leeches with occult science, transforming the creatures into living blood bags. While these bloodletting techniques are of dubious therapeutic value to patients, they make an effective method for collecting samples from lessthan-willing subjects.

Though often benign in nature, these bloated leeches can be turned to violent purpose by an apothecary willing to use the creatures in such a manner. During combat, an apothecary may dispatch the leeches against their foes, then call the creatures back to themselves to heal using their foe's blood.

entries.name: Blood Leeches

entries: The black, plump wriggling form of the leech squirms and crawls. Its oily, slick skin is wet and slippery. It lets out a high-pitched screech as it lunges towards its prey.

Leeches are a common creature kept in large quantities in apothecaries' laboratories. Aside from their standard practical uses of bloodletting and transfusions, they have also been the subjects of early apothecary experimentation. Different forms of leeches have been designed to better suit apothecaries' needs. Some Alienists have designed leeches that attach directly to the brain stem, allowing the leech to eat the intellect and thoughts of other creatures. Mutagenists have designed leeches that can harness the arcane energies found in mageborn blood.

items: {@b Leech Variants:} Ambitious apothecaries have used leeches in different ways. There are two mutant variations of the Blood Leech.

entries.name: Combat Tactics

monsterFluff.name: Body Snatcher

entries: This patchwork monster of stitched-together corpses oozes black ichor from its seams. The figure is a hulking form, about 7 feet tall with broad shoulders and a hunched back. Its head seems small compared to its body, with pale white eyes highlighting sunken dark sockets. A lipless mouth forces the creature into a constant menacing grimace. Draped in a thick black trench coat and wide brimmed hat while smelling of sulfur and brimstone, the unsettling humming and mumbling of the creature echoes in the ears of those it is about to grab. The most unsettling feature is the creature's four arms, which end in massive, oversized hands, each with eight long, spindly fingers. The creature shifts from shadow to shadow effortlessly, in a haunting ghost-like fashion unusual for its size.

Stitched together from the remains of numerous corpses and animated through forbidden alchemical processes, the Body Snatcher roams the darkness. Created by a deranged doctor to abduct subjects for gruesome experiments, it lingers in shadows, waiting for unwary travelers to seize and vanish into the night.

Empowered by the night, the Body Snatcher uses shadow to drain the vitality and energy of those it grabs, weakening them as they attempt to resist and escape. Shadows wrap around it, helping it hold its victims in place while it absconds with them into the darkest corners of the night

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Body Snatcher sticks to dimly lit areas or places of complete darkness. It teleports up to a creature and attempts to grapple it, teleporting away as soon as it has one or two targets in its hands. Often the Body Snatcher will emerge from tunnels or secret entrances to its lair. They do not travel far from the labs they were created in and often have easy points of escape to disappear once they have a victim in hand.

monsterFluff.name: Bojack

entries: This creature, which appears to be a dead horse flopped on its back, convulses and its stomach suddenly splits open, exposing its intestines and organs. Long, spindly, arachnid-like legs violently sprout from its torso as its stomach opens into a maw filled with sharp jagged teeth formed from the splayed rib cage of the beast. The horse legs limply hang in the air, as the creature skitters towards you with intense speed, intestines flapping around its maw like a sickly tongue. The head of the horse dangles lifelessly, but its mouth still gnashes and salivates acidic bile.

Many valiant warriors have ridden into Drakkenheim mounted on a loyal steed, not realizing that the rubble and wreckage filling the streets makes the ruins an unsuitable environment for a horse. Often, these poor animals must be abandoned not long after entering the ruins, injured from the unstable terrain. Prime targets for other predators, the horses are often tragically slaughtered. However, when their corpses are left behind, a parasite-like mutation festers within them, causing their skin to erupt with spider-like limbs, pincers, and maws.

Disguising themselves as mere corpses strewn across the dark and misty streets of the ruined city, one can hardly differentiate a Bojack from a dead horse. With their spider limbs they can scurry along walls and ceilings with ease, and barely make a sound. They move with lightning-fast speed, able to scuttle across a city street in mere seconds. This terrifying speed, ease of traversing the terrain, and ability to disguise itself have made them a deadly threat to adventurers in the city.

One of the most horrifying recorded encounters with Bojacks in Drakkenheim came from an early report from Hooded Lantern scouts investigating old stables south of Champion's Gate near the city outskirts. They reported finding "piles of dead horses buzzing with large, mutated flies feasting on the meat." The report goes on to speak of several of the horse corpses suddenly "bursting open" with "insectoid legs and a horrible maw formed from the splayed rib cage of the dead beasts." The report describes the speed and ferocity displayed in the immediate strike, with nearly an entire squad of eight Hooded Lantern scouts ripped to shreds in only a matter of seconds while the remaining Lanterns fled back out of the city.

One of the surviving Hooded Lanterns, Sten Livingston Sr., was brave enough to volunteer to lead the following expedition into the ruins. On the road into the city a dead and bloated horse corpse lay on the side of the road. Livingston stopped his troops and approached the beast with weapons drawn, kicking the corpse to check if it would spring to life. The corpse remained motionless. It has since become a tradition spread through the Lanterns, and even into new adventuring parties, to kick the horse on the way into Drakkenheim. Many have chalked this up to a sign of good luck, not realizing the harrowing story and the lives lost that caused this strange tradition.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Bojack is an ambush skirmisher. It waits for the opportune moment to strike, attempting to surprise as many targets as possible. After it surprises its prey, it attacks with its Impaling Limbs or Corrosive Mucus and uses its Predatory Cunning to move out of melee range.

The Bojack can climb walls and will try and skitter up buildings or behind walls, springing back out to attack before escaping again. If brought below 20 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, the Bojack attempts to {@action Dash|XPHB} away and {@action Hide|XPHB}.

monsterFluff.name: Cacophonous Chimera

entries: The Cacophonous Chimera's three heads include a chittering rat, a screeching harpy, and a howling garmyr, which together perform a madness-inducing chorus as they slaughter their prey. Its forelimbs are clawed rat-like paws, its rear legs are avian talons, and the beast's colossal furry body is borne upon massive wings of blood-red feathers with a slithering lamprey eel for a tail.

The Cacophonous Chimera emerged from a catastrophic convergence of several creatures — a Garmyr, Deep Dreg, Manticore, Ratling, and a Harpy — amidst a fierce battle. Caught in a terrible arcane anomaly, these creatures were unwillingly combined into this single, horrific form. Each head retains the memories and instincts of its original form, driving the chimera in a constant battle for dominance and survival. This relentless conflict within itself fuels its madness and aggression towards anything it encounters in the ruins.

The Cacophonous Chimera lives in a constant state of internal discord as its three heads, each with its own predatory instincts, vie for control over its body. The constant bickering and screaming among the heads produce a sound that reverberates painfully within the skulls of all who hear it, inducing terror, confusion, and madness. Depending on which head momentarily gains dominance, the tone and effect of their combined shrieking varies, leaving their prey disoriented and defenseless.

This terror hunts throughout the Outer City, making lairs within the crumbling ruins of the Spokes Merchant's Exchange. The main tower was one of the tallest buildings outside Drakkenheim's walls and functioned as a hub for traders and local craftspeople to conduct business without needing to travel to the bustling market square of the Inner City. The structure has become a ramshackle ruin, the crooked spire compromised by the constant shrieking of the chimera. Still, this strategic perch not only provides an ideal vantage point for the monstrosity. The structural damage also dissuades other monsters and adventurers from intruding on the chimera's personal domain.

entries.name: Roleplaying Traits
entries: The following traits can be used to inspire roleplaying the Cacophonous Chimera:

items: {@b Personality Trait:} "Just ONCE can we chat with someone a little before we eat them? RARGH! STOP TALKING! RIP AND TEAR! NO! NO! NO! Our stomach is FOUR TIMES bigger than it used to be! I'm STARVING!"
{@b Bond:} "We're fused together. Although each of us wants to be separated, in truth we're afraid of what would happen if we were ever torn apart."
{@b Ideal:} "I make such wonderful music! Each howl, shriek, and chitter resonates to form a deadly orchestra. I can't stand silence!"
{@b Flaw:} "We're constantly arguing. Our internal strife often distracts us from opportunities or leads us into traps, as we can't agree even on the simplest decisions."

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they {@action Study|XPHB} a Cacophonous Chimera, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (15+) Freakish Fusion
entries: You're aware of the chimera's Epic Resistance Epic Action.

entries.name: (20+) Fighting for Control
entries: You recognize the chimera's Cacophony Epic Action, noting that if the creature could be silenced, it would be far less formidable.

entries.name: (25+) Powerful but Distracted
entries: You understand its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Desperate to eat and consume, the Cacophonous Chimera viciously attacks prey on sight despite the desires of its harpy head to engage in a little conversation first. The Cacophonous Chimera is not a very subtle hunter. Its prey can hear it coming by the sound of its droning cacophony from at least a city block away, which may give them opportunity to prepare, hide, or flee.

The range of its Cacophony can affect creatures before they can see the chimera itself. By the time the chimera arrives, its prey may be shaken and immobilized by the sound. Depending on how ravenous and furious it is, the chimera closes with its prey and tears them apart using its Claws, Bite, and Tail.

Against a target that shows resilience to its cacophony or who retaliates with formidable attacks of their own, the chimera keeps a middle distance, trying to keep out of melee range while leaving its foes in its Cacophonous Chorus aura. However, its ravenous Garmyr head and Ratling head can often get in the way of the better judgment here, prompting the chimera to engage in melee even when it would not be advantageous.

Furthermore, the three creatures are generally too busy arguing or overconfident to think twice about the actual danger and stakes they might be facing, and so may need to be grievously wounded before fleeing is an option.

items.name: Lieutenant Petra & Captain Ansom Lang

entries: Petra Lang is a fit and nimble teenager with long black hair, a narrow, pointed chin, and bold features. She wears the Lanterns' hooded green cloak and light {@item studded leather armor|XPHB} with a lieutenant's insignia on her shoulder pauldron.

Ansom Lang is an athletic teenager with long black hair and a short neat beard, angular jaw, and rugged features. He is garbed in a hooded green cloak and {@item studded leather armor|XPHB} of the Hooded Lanterns that prominently displays a captain's insignia on his shoulder

Petra, the youngest of the two, has spent most of her life training under the Hooded Lanterns. She prides herself on her marksmanship and scavenging, and knows she is looked up to by many of the soldiers. She is a proud and friendly commander who the troops are happy to follow.
Ansom plans to become the Lord Commander once Elias retires. He is a stern commander who leads by example, displaying incredible discipline and unwavering loyalty to his adopted father

entries.name: Personality Trait
entries: I have been in Drakkenheim long enough to know not to trust anyone. I am extremely wary of adventurers, and anyone who might cause problems for the Lanterns.

entries.name: Ideal
entries: I believe that if my sister and I work hard enough, with the right people, that maybe we can change things.

entries.name: Bond
entries: Myself and Petra have had each other's backs since we were children. That will never change.

entries.name: Flaw
entries: I find reasons to not like people, and find reasons to doubt the commitment of the people around me.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Petra is a skilled archer and skirmisher. She prefers to keep her foes at range to gain a vantage point over them in combat. She is a cunning scout who is more likely to set up an ambush than attack directly. When pinned down, she tries to move out of melee into a more advantageous position. If she is low on options, she attempts to escape.

Ansom is a skilled swordsman who prefers to engage his foes in melee combat. He typically starts combat from a good vantage point by attacking with his bow and then moving closer to unleash a flurry of sword attacks. He is a confident and aggressive, and has pushed the Hooded Lanterns through many decisive victories over the horrors of Drakkenheim.
Ansom has enough sense to know when a combat encounter is threatening to cost the lives of his unit, and will fall back or retreat if his instincts tell him it is the better move.
Nothing like family to keep you honest. That and a sword that makes you tell the truth.

Given the strange features of this massive, muscled, eight-foot-tall figure, it is difficult to say if it was once human or a troll. Its bruised skin stretches and rips over barely contained muscles. It is pin-headed, with an emotionless face, glassy-eyes, and a slack-jawed maw.

Most disturbingly, its ribcage is splayed open, revealing guts and viscera along with a smaller, vestigial creature with wrinkled flesh and a mewling mouth. It holds its sticklike arms and curled fingers close, and its neck can barley hold its massive head. Thin translucent skin covers its huge brain, the blood vessels within softly glowing. Raising its tiny hands to its temples, its eyes bulge and its face contorts into a twisted expression.

The Cerebrograft is a horrific attempt to combine two creatures into a singular form, a nightmarish combination of brains and brawn. Through surgical implantation and flesh-melding, an apothecary creates a forced symbiosis, fusing their nervous systems and unlocking potent psionic abilities.

entries.name: Improved Lackeys
entries: A Cerebrograft is often the "reward" granted to a pair of loyal lab assistants, a means of "removing deficiencies" by combining their bodies and minds, frequently named a portmanteau of its constituent beings.

entries.name: Dominant Personality
entries: Although intended to be a symbiosis of two minds, typically, the implanted creature subsumes the psyche of its host, fully controling the new form. However, sometimes, the two beings form a constituent mind combining elements of the originals, or even a bicameral mind where the original two debate internally over what action to take.

entries.name: Delicate Work
entries: Thanks to their psionic abilities, Cerebrografts are well suited to controlling other test subjects. Apothecaries find their precise telekinetic powers especially useful in surgical procedures and laboratory experiments.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Medicine|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to Study a Cerebrograft, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (10+) Occult Fleshmending
entries: You uncover the Cerebrograft's Dual Minds trait.

entries.name: (15+) Powerful Psionics
entries: You recognize its Telekinetic Grip and Psychic Crush.

entries.name: (20+) Powerful, Clumsy, and Slow
entries: You learn the Cerebrograft's ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Despite its physical and psionic might, Cerebrografts prefers fighting alongside allies of its apothecary master. When confronted with multiple foes, it tries to overwhelm their minds using Psychic Crush to escape and find reinforcements.

A Cerebrograft uses its Telekinetic Grip to hold its enemies, unruly test subjects, and wild experiments at bay. It typically focuses on one target, allowing allies to pummel the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} foe. If it can, it uses the environment to its advantage, moving foes to restrain them such as into mancles, cages, or surgery tables.
