The figure is garbed in large safety goggles, an acid-burned thick lab apron, white chemical-stained lab coat, and rubber gloves. The skin on their face is the only visible flesh on them, scarred by bubbling chemical burns.

Chemists indulge in the science of the alchemical, often harnessing the raw potential of elemental formulae while creating unique compounds and reagents. They have been known to dabble in the science behind the creation of elementals and oozes, and perfecting explosives and acids.

entries.name: Chemist Minions
entries: Although Chemists often do not dabble in creating creatures, any apothecary can make use of minions. Simple elementals and oozes can be found in a Chemist's lab. {@creature Tanker|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Tankers} work as a good lab assistant for administering large amounts of chemical formulae for the scientist, while {@creature Living Biohazard|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Living Biohazards} are often the failed early experiments many Chemists. A {@creature Chemystral|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} is the ultimate pride and joy of many chemists.

items: {@b Personality Trait:} I revel in the chaos and destruction that my concoctions cause, watching the flames and corrosion with maniacal laughter and a crazed gleam in my eyes.
{@b Bond:} Creativity is born from chaos; the most groundbreaking discoveries require pushing boundaries, no matter the dangers involved.
{@b Ideal:} I am obsessed with avenging my mentor, who was persecuted by those who feared our knowledge and power.

{@b Flaw:} My obsession with perfecting destructive formulae often leads me to take careless risks, sabotaging my own work and safety. I've burned down my own workshop more times than I can remember, and I'll do it again.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Medicine|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to {@action study|XPHB} a Chemist, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (10+) Resistance from Exposure
entries: You know of the Chemist's damage {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (15+) Masters of Compounds
entries: You learn the Chemist's Critical {@variantrule Condition|XPHB} trait and Explosive Compound action. (20+) Mental, not Physical, Prowess. You are aware of the Chemist's AC and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Chemists opt to start things off with a bang, unleashing their Explosive Concoction on the first round, especially against a grouped together party. They use Acid Rain to create a dangerous zone between them and their enemies and default to unleashing their Chemical Spray on enemies stuck in the difficult area. If a creature closes the distance on the Chemist, they use their Caustic Grip. If they find themselves surrounded or outnumbered in close quarters, they attempt to escape.
The only chemists I admire are the ones who make Caspian cinnamon rolls. This is not one of them.

This massive, undulating chemical ooze shimmers in hues of blue, green, pink, and purple. Its large amorphous form throbs and wobbles as it alters its composition constantly to adapt to its surrounding environments. Everything the blob touches dissolves quickly within its form. The distinct smell of bile and stomach acid surround it.

One of a {@creature Chemist|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}'s ultimate creations, the Chemystral is a perfectly balanced sentient compound capable of altering its physiology to adapt to surrounding threats. The horrific ooze has the ability to stick to any surface and even propel itself into the air and fly. It is impervious to nearly all forms of elemental attack. Much like a chameleon changing its color to blend into its surroundings, the Chemystral changes itself at a cellular level to adapt to environmental changes and elemental threats, gaining properties to better combat predators. Even with its inherent resilience, the Chemystral is unable to adapt to the cold, or deal with intense sound.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Chemystral attempts to Engulf as many victims as it can. It cares little about taking elemental damage and only thinks to retreat if it is consistently taking Cold damage.

monsterFluff.name: Chitinous Dreg

entries: The body and face of this mutated wretch is covered in thick, knobby bone plates that have torn violently through their flesh. The exposed ribs of their chest have fused together into a single plate, forming an armor-like appearance. Past their elbow, the muscle and sinew of their forelimbs hangs limply from their protruding exposed bones, which have been reshaped into long, serrated bone-blades caked with gore.

These Dregs have heavy mutations to their bone structure which covers them in a plated exoskeleton. Able to shrug off most attacks, Chitinous Dregs charge into battle, using their jagged forearm bone blades in a frenzy of ferocious strikes upon their prey.

entries.name: Study the Foe

entries.name: (15+) Sturdy Foe
entries: You are aware of the Chitinous Dreg's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Chitinous Dregs often charge into the front lines of combat. It positions itself between other Dregs and their foes almost as if it was defending its allies. Chitinous Dregs attempt to draw the combat towards itself at all times, using its Bone Blades to keep the focus on it, and its Sentinel Strike Reaction and No Escape trait to ensure creatures facing it cannot get away. The Chitinous Dreg is a warrior and rarely retreats: it is too enraged with a protective bloodlust when thrust into battle to worry about its own wellbeing.

monsterFluff.name: Chitter

entries: Scampering up the wall is a creature the size of a hound. It resembles a mostly hairless squirrel save for its bushy tail and patchy tufts of mottled fur. Its eyes are glassy and milk white, and its mouth seems almost human, sporting huge, pearly white teeth that grin maniacally. It frantically clambers upward, while chittering a maddening chorus with its clacking teeth.

The Queen's Park Gardens are one of the most heavily contaminated areas in the city. Its massive gardens and trails were once a place of lush beauty, thick with trees, floral arrangements, topiary masterpieces, tranquil groves, and an abundance of wildlife. Drakkenheim's contamination warped all things, monstrously changing the creatures within. Now even the squirrels, which occupied the gardens in large numbers, are feral and mutated. Those wandering forested areas should be wary of chittering sounds echoing through the trees. These monsters attack in numbers, their clacking teeth maddening those nearby. The once friendly squirrels that locals would stop to feed now feed whether you want them to or not.

Chitters are also encountered along the heavily wooded northern outskirts of Drakkenheim and much of the farmlands surrounding the city. These places are not free from contamination; Chitters have been seen roaming like packs of feral dogs through the fields or lurking near woods. Chitters now occasionally roam the streets in the center of the city, climbing towers and buildings before leaping down onto their prey. No longer confined to the gardens, the city is their hunting ground and its ruins make wonderful homes for packs of Chitters.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Chitter, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Wall Crawling
entries: You are aware of its {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB}, its Running Leap trait, and its Slow Fall feature.

entries.name: (10+) Madding Noise
entries: You know of its Chitter attack action.

entries.name: (15+) Simple Minded
entries: You recognize its mental ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Chitters often attack in a small group. Usually two to three that form a family will stick together. The mutated squirrels have been known to be quite territorial and hostile, even to other Chitter families who try to infringe on their territory.

Chitters are excellent climbers, capable of falling a great distance without fear of hurting themselves. It is not uncommon for Chitters to be found in tall buildings, or up on the top floor of ruined houses, or hard-to-reach rooftops or attics. Chitters charge their enemies and leap at them, attempting to disable them with their chittering, and relying on their Claws and Bite. Chitters protect their homes with determined ferocity, but if reduced to less than a third of their Hit Points, they leap and clamber away.

items.name: Congregation

entries: A crowd of pilgrims brandish clubs, torches, and pitchforks. They begin to muster up courage, spouting out passages from the writings of the Falling Fire, calling out the blasphemous to be brought low by the fires to cleanse them of their sins.

The Followers of the Falling Fire gather in great throngs filled with fiery passion, lighting their torches and lanterns and taking up whatever they can find as a weapon. When the zealous masses flood the streets, the crowd becomes more than a match for the mightiest warriors.
Three's a crowd and coincidentally the number of prongs you get stabbed with. People get too excited in groups.

monsterFluff.name: Crater Wurm

entries: The earth trembles, vibrating pebbles and dust. A deep rumble wells from below. Suddenly, stone cracks, extruding a titanic wurm. It rears its massive head, opening a petal-like mouth filled with long jagged crystalline teeth all pointed into its throat. Its body is covered in muddy purple plates with octarine spines jutting from between. Its hot breath sends octarine slime flying as it dives toward you.

Those who dared venture into the Crater Basin returned with harrowing tales of the tremendous Crater Wurms. They describe the earth shaking moments before a gargantuan wurm breaches the surface, swallowing creatures in its path. Curiously, the wurms are only seen in the desolate crater. Few understand how such gigantic creatures, let alone multiple wurms, can survive here, or why they do not leave to hunt elsewhere.

In truth, Crater Wurms mainly subsist on inorganic minerals found in the dirt, mud, and rock they burrow through, requiring little organic matter. The wurm's gullet functions like a contaminated crucible: minerals, rock, and living matter are broken down and crystallized, with delerium expelled as waste. Crater Wurms spend most of their lives underground, creating miles of twisting tunnels filled with glittering delerium, only surfacing in the Crater Basin to reproduce. Though none have yet seen the event, the wurm's massive form splits, releasing young from the carcass.

Perhaps no creature in Drakkenheim is more responsible for the deeply rooted contamination than Crater Wurms. The continued existence of these monsters could see the world transform into a contaminated wasteland. Tunneling below the surface, they have spread contamination deep into the bowels of the earth. Indeed, all the crystals scattered across the surface, the rich veins of delerium near the Scar, and the great deposits around the Crater itself pale in comparison to the mass of delerium left buried far underground by the Crater Wurms.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they {@action Study|XPHB} a Crater Wurm, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (15+) Subterranean Threat
entries: You know it has {@sense Tremorsense|XPHB} and that it creates tunnels when digging through rock.

entries.name: (20+) Earth Shaker
entries: You're aware of the Crater Wurms' Breach and Bite attacks.

entries.name: (25+) Blunderous Brute
entries: You recognize the Crater Wurms' strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Crater Wurms disregard other creatures, viewing them as only morsels to consume. All are as the dust of the earth to it—simply food. These wurms understand that creatures they devour often try to flee. Their favored tactic is to remain buried until their {@sense Tremorsense|XPHB} detects movement. They then surface with its Breach action, making Bite attacks, swallowing nearby {@condition Prone|XPHB} creatures. They dive beneath the ground once at least one creature is swallowed, or if reduced to half its Hit Point maximum.

monsterFluff.name: Crimson Countess
entries: The Crimson Countess is a powerful queen of harpies. Her red-feathered wings and deep crimson hair set her apart from the many harpy followers she commands. She is clad is black and gold armor and carries with her a spear that crackles with magical energies. Her hands and feet are black talons with sharp claws. The Crimson Countess is a cunning hunter and territorial to the Clock Tower. She has staked her claim over the center of the city, and hunts the various monsters and misguided faction agents who come close.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Countess only leaves her clock tower to join in on hunts with her valkyries, but otherwise she prefers the defendable position at the towers highest floor. From here any adventurer who makes it past her soldiers and into her lair can easily be grabbed and thrown off the open balconies, falling to their death.

She is overconfident and will do anything to protect her advantageous position in the city. She only flees if all her minions are dead and she is below 25 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If she flees, she will attempt to gather more soldiers and return to reclaim the clock tower at a later date.

monsterFluff.name: Crimson Knight

entries: Clad in blackened steel armor accented in red, this knight wears the marks of their vampiric master emblazoned upon their tower shield. They carry an axe that crackles with red energy; their blood red eyes peer out from their helmet, fangs visible and hungry.

The Crimson Knights are formidable vampire spawn, meticulously trained as elite house soldiers and personal bodyguards for their vampiric masters. These fierce warriors are inextricably bound to serve their lords with unwavering loyalty, showing little interest in advancing beyond their designated roles. Instead, they derive immense satisfaction from the carnage they unleash in honor of their household and liege.

Proud of their exceptional combat skills, the Crimson Knights devote their eternal lives almost exclusively to honing their martial prowess. Their existence is characterized by relentless training and preparation, making them adept in various forms of battle. This rigorous focus on combat not only sharpens their abilities but also fuels their insatiable thirst for the chaos of warfare.

In the heat of battle, the Crimson Knights are at their most formidable. They hunger for the bloodshed that accompanies fierce engagements, and they sustain themselves by feeding on the blood of those they defeat. To fight is to feed for these knights, and their hunger is perpetual, driving them to seek out conflict where they can showcase their deadly skills and quench their relentless thirst.

entries.name: (10+) Elite Spawn
entries: You know the Crimson Knight's damage {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}.

entries.name: (15+) Unholy Magic
entries: You recognize the Crimson Knight can unleash a variety of powerful smites.

entries.name: (20+) Weaknesses
entries: You are aware the vampire's regeneration is temporarily halted by Radiant damage, and its Vampire Weaknesses.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Crimson Knights form units with other minions and thralls of their vampire masters. Several Crimson Knights may form an elite guard, or one might be attached to lead a contingent of vampire thralls.

In battle, Crimson Knights seek out the most formidable melee combatants to meet head on, disarming them with Crackling Smite. They make use of Unholy Smite to prevent their target from healing, and terrorize them using Wrathful Smite.

A Crimson Knight will give their undead existence to defend their master and hold fast even as they are cut down. If they encounter a foe capable of dealing Radiant damage, they make them the target of their attacks to ensure they can continue to regenerate.

items.name: Crypt-Starved Vladimir von Drakken

entries: Before you stands an emaciated undead man. He looks downward, with sallow red-glowing eyes hidden behind a mass of long, matted black hair. His nose is rotted and gone, his flesh cracked and decayed, and his bent pose a far cry from the imperial majesty he possessed and lost so long ago. He is swathed only in an ancient burial shroud and wrappings worn like a robe. Across his neck, a prominent and wretched scar marks how his head was sewn back upon his shoulders. He drags an ancient obsidian greatsword behind him, holding the weapon by its blade as a thin trickle of blood seeps from his fingers. From his back emerge the broken stumps of clipped wings, now little more than useless limbs of tattered gore. Yet, there is a quiet, primal power thrumming within his form.

When returned to unlife via the Sanguine Rite, Vladimir von Drakken first manifests in this form. He remains in this form until he has fed on enough individuals of sufficient power, upon which he assumes his Reborn form.

Although he cannot be permanently destroyed in this form, Vladimir von Drakken is greatly {@condition weakened|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} in this state and desires nothing more than returning to his full power.

monsterFluff.name: Crystalline Dreg

entries: The creature's jagged features make them appear to be made from shattered glass. Their flesh is a fractal arrangement of polygonal angles of shimmering crystal. Throughout their body, sharp jutting shards extend and retract as they move towards you, their body pulling in and refracting light at odd angles and with an increased intensity.

Much in the manner that some buildings closer to the meteor site had their fundamental elements changed in bizarre ways, such as stone and wood being transformed into flesh or glass, these Dregs have had their flesh warped into hard crystal. They have an innate ability to pull in light and the elements, briefly storing them in their form before expelling them in a manner that uses their body as a focusing lens, increasing the potency of these forces.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Crystalline Dreg is quite literally a glass cannon. It prefers to stay behind other Dregs, blasting its foes with its beam attacks and absorbing any elemental damage to alter its attacks. If an enemy who can deal Bludgeoning damage is present, the Crystalline Dreg will flee from that creature and attempt to kill them from a distance, knowing it is their biggest threat. The Dreg tends to focus on enemies approaching with melee weapons over anyone using elemental damage. If the front line of Dregs that the Crystalline Dreg often uses as shield is gone, or if the Crystalline Dregs are outnumbered and threatened with melee combat, they attempt to flee.

monsterFluff.name: Cyclopean Hulk

entries: Tall and lithe, this Haze Hulk's body is uniquely marked by taut muscles and pronounced blood vessels beneath its semi-translucent skin, which shows occasional fissures from the intense eldritch power contained within. Its elongated face is dominated by a single, malevolent cyclopean eye that glows like a lantern in the dark of the ruins.

Cyclopean Hulks have developed a singular eye as a focal point for the contaminated energy stored in their body, which they unleash as a destructive beam. They also have the unique ability to close their eye and wink out of their plane of existence temporarily, somehow triggering an arcane temporal rift using their focused magic

The Cyclopean Hulk focuses its power on blasting enemies from afar or slamming them into the ground if they get close. It will then Wink out of existence, reappearing every few seconds to deliver a devastating blast from its eye before vanishing again. Cyclopean Hulks usually fight to the end, and rarely flee.

monsterFluff.name: Dark Confessor

entries: Dressed in robes of black and red that stand as a mockery to the garb often worn by members of the Sacred Flame, and clutching an ornate golden staff with a crimson orb in one hand, and a shimmering spectral maul in the other, these Dark Confessors call forth unholy curses and spirits from the abyss to bend to their will. Their pale skin, sunken black eyes, and sharp fangs stand as a grim reminder that even the holy can succumb to the whims of vampiric lords.

When the Court of the Night seeks to infiltrate a community, their first priority is to corrupt its leaders, especially their most bitter rivals in the Faith of the Sacred Flame. Thus, the flamekeepers or local priests are often targeted in particular to be transformed into vampire spawn. When these devout worshipers become vampire spawn, they are known as Dark Confessors. Their divine powers twist and warp into dark, corrupted magic under the influence of vampiric forces. In undeath, they channel that same potent energy, now converted into terrifying vampiric sorcery, which they wield to serve their masters. As Dark Confessors, they lead sinister rites and unholy rituals, gathering more followers to the cause of their vampiric overlords.

With their natural authority and sway over commonfolk, Dark Confessors manipulate communities to fall under the influence of vampire lords. They often foster cult-like followings, leading the people into pledging allegiance to their dark masters. These cults believe that by proving their loyalty, they might escape the curse of undeath and servitude. Entire towns and villages have succumbed to the charismatic influence of a Dark Confessor, their inhabitants abandoning former beliefs and swearing unwavering fealty to their vampire lords, hoping this grim devotion will save them from a far worse fate.

If there are enemies grouped close to one another, the Dark
Confessor uses Unholy Light on them.
The Dark Confessor flees if it is below 50 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or takes steady Radiant damage.

monsterFluff.name: Dark Growth

entries: The remains of a corpse is splayed across a ruined wall. A chaotic mass of jet-black brambles and vines pours from its torso, clinging to the nearby stonework. Branches have burst from its form, and its neck erupts into another mass of plant matter. The skull is severed from the body with its jaw unhinged and hanging in a horrible expression, stuck in place by the writhing vines. Throughout this Dark Growth, flowers bloom in iridescent neon hues and the smell of sweet pollen and decaying flesh fills the air. You hear gentle whispers from a distant voice, distinctly familiar and beckoning.

{@condition Contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} causes most plants to wither and die, but some thrive on it, absorbing water and delerium from the soil to mutate into deadly flora. In Drakkenheim's urban wasteland, suitable plots of fertile soil are scarce outside {@link Queen's Park Garden}, necessitating a creative adaptation to proliferate. These Dark Growths take root in the bodies of creatures through their infectious, delerium-infused spores.

Emitted from their blooming flowers, these spores drift silently throughout the air until they enter another creature's body through the ears, mouth, or nose. Once inside, these spores can lay dormant for some time, slowly contaminating their host with internal mutation which slowly decay their flesh and bone from within, transforming it into an ideal place for the Dark Growth to germinate. When the creature succumbs to contamination, or dies with the spores within it, the plant awakens. Consuming the internal organs of the dying infected, it suddenly and violently sprouts. Often, this transformation occurs so suddenly that the creature remains walking around, the Dark Growth using the corpse as a mobile shell so it may plant in an ideal location to spread future spores.

One apothecary reports a case where a knight returning from a mission into the Inner City had survived the journey relatively unscathed save for an excursion into the gardens where a puff of what they thought was pollen from strange iridescent flowers got in their eyes. The knight thought little of it, suffering no immediate effects. After returning to Emberwood, the knight complained of stomach cramps, nausea, and headaches, eventually passing out from the pain. The apothecary performed an emergency surgery, cutting the patient open only to have their intestines burst out like a barrage of meaty, thorn-covered brambles that attempted to strangle the apothecary. Their intestines had been completely replaced with plant matter that had fused into their guts.

entries.name: Study the Foe

entries.name: (15+) Kill it with fire!

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: A Dark Growth is a simple-minded plant. It uses Mimicry to lure passing creatures towards it, often mimicking the sounds of children or people in need. It entangles and infests any target near it, infecting it with its spores. The creature is a stationary plant and does not flee.

monsterFluff.name: Dark Growth Shambler

entries: Staggering from the shadows is a gaunt humanoid with pale flesh and a hunched form. Vines and branches protrude from its gaping mouth and push through its flesh throughout its body. Flowers emerge from these growths, blooming in iridescent neon hues. A smell of sweet sugar and decaying flesh fills the air, and whispers begin to issue from it even though the creature's mouth doesn't move.

Sometimes, when the body of one infected with {@creature Dark Growth|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Dark Growths} bursts open in the moment of their death, the body does not immediately collapse and decay. Instead, the creature shambles around, its body still intact, but with vines and thorny black branches bursting from its eye sockets, mouth, and flesh, its body now a protective shell for the plant within.

monsterFluff.name: Deep Dreg Warrior

entries: Emerging from the contaminated waters is a humanoid figure with disturbing piscine mutations. Their body is covered in glittering scales of sea green, midnight purple, and deep blue. Their monstrous face has two large, bulbous eyes and a gaping, fishlike mouth filled with oddly-shaped teeth—a mixture of humanoid, shark, and other aquatic animals. Spindly, fleshy whiskers surround their fish lips. They have webbed feet and hands, and thin fins jut from their arms, legs, and face. They wear little more than ragged clothing and scraps of leather armor, and carry a brace of javelins, a spear, and a fishing net.

Dwelling in the contaminated sewers and waterways of Drakkenheim, a Deep Dreg Warrior is left with only dim memories of their former lives, their identities are fully subsumed by eldritch contamination and thralldom to the Duchess. Nevertheless, many describe their state as preferable to the lives they lived before, describing unfortunate humans as cursed landwalkers who must be "freed.".

entries.name: (15+) Strong and Tough

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Deep Dreg Warriors attack from the water, throwing their spears and diving back under the surface as added protection against ranged retaliation. When they engage in melee, the warriors use their Net to restrain their foes, and make melee attacks (with the bonus damage from Catch of the Day) to knock them {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}.

Deep Dregs Warriors flee whenever they are outnumbered or if they are reduced below half their maximum {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. They swim to safety rather than die fighting, and prefer to fall back and retaliate after gathering reinforcements.

monsterFluff.name: Deep Knight

entries: Towering over the other Deep Dregs is a muscle-bound warrior with a head shaped like a hammerhead shark. They carry a colossal shield made from the opalescent shell of some mollusk, and their gnarled hide is covered in algae and barnacles. A thick chain is wrapped around their wrists, attached to the massive, spiked harpoon they carry.

Champions of the Duchess, Deep Knights tower over others of their kind. They lead groups of Deep Dreg Warriors on excursions and important missions. The Duchess keeps a contingent of Deep Knights as her personal honor guard to protect her lair.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Deep Knight is the forward assault of the Deep Dregs and uses their seashell shields to deflect attacks and their harpoons to pull enemies into close range before biting them with their shark teeth.
The Deep Knight will defend the other Deep Dregs to the death. If it is the last one standing it will attempt to flee, but as long as there are allies to protect, it will stay and fight.

monsterFluff.name: Deep Siren

entries: This a wretched, mutated crone has sea-green hair and blue-gray flesh, and is garbed in a gown of algae and kelp. They carry pouches filled with occult reagents, and vials filled with a strange octarine goo. Despite their appearance, as they speak their words are no less honeyed and sweet.

Spellcasters transformed by the Duchess's influence become Deep Sirens, retaining a measure of their magical abilities. These sirens will act as forward generals or confidants for the Duchess, and often a well-regarded siren will act as her personal court mage.

entries: Deep Sirens are the generals and confidants to the Duchess and often serve as the eyes and ears of their mistress. They use their Illusory Appearance to walk among humanoids and observe them, planning and plotting the attacks of the Deep Dregs. Once it has gathered information, a Deep Siren returns to the Duchess, and is often sent with the Deep Dregs to storm beaches, infiltrate sewers, or take over cities on stormy nights.
The siren doesn't like being in close combat, and always attempts to use {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} to move to a more beneficial position, then unleash Storm Lash or spellcasting upon their foes.
They flee if surrounded, if outnumbered, or if they feel the battle is not going in their favor.

A wyrmling usually does not yet fully understand their transtemporal senses, and experiences memories of their adulthood and future in dreams and visions.

entries.name: Delerium Dragons

entries: This unearthly dragon is a crystalline horror, its body formed from angular gem-like scales pulsing with octarine light. Its form is raw delerium. Each scale is a gleaming crystal refracting light into eerie hues of purple, yellow, and green, with an unnatural sharpness that feels both fragile and impossibly durable.

The dragon's wings are translucent and webbed with glowing crystal veins that shimmer, casting kaleidoscopic patterns as it moves. Each beat causes the air to hum, vibrating with a chaotic energy that overwhelms and distorts the senses. Each step the dragon takes leaves delicate motes of crystal growing into jagged formations, tainting the landscape. Its eyes are like multifaceted gems, swirling with chaotic magic pooling within their depths. The beast's crystalline horns and talons are razor-sharp, gleaming like polished jewels, yet crackling with eldritch energy.

Inscrutable beings of the Space Between Worlds, Delerium Dragons are order from chaos incarnate. How such creatures came to be is unknown, and few know of their existence. Some propose that they emerged spontaneously, hatching from crystalline eggs with octarine shells.

A Delerium Dragon is not simply contaminated, but a unique type of gemstone dragon with an otherworldly physiology. These dragons are literally made of the crystals: their claws, bones, and scales are refracting {@item shard|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium shard}. Their flesh and organs are incomprehensible organic matter, and their blood is delerium sludge. When unleashings its breath weapon, it exhales a storm of glittering shards that explode, causing madness, mutation, and wild magic to erupt in the area.

Delerium Dragons are amongst the most powerful beings born within the Space Between Worlds. Capable of perceiving dimensions imperceptible to mortals, these dragons often seem flighty or {@condition distracted|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, but this is because they experience layers of reality which humans cannot. They are thus strange intermediaries, able to interact with creatures on a transdimensional level. Indeed, Delerium Dragons are unstuck in time, unrestrained by the linear progression of past, present, and future. Some experience their entire lives simultaneously, whereas others live their lives non-sequentially. Most understand that even their own existences is beyond comprehension, and many contemplate the fundamental nature of existence, chaos, and the cosmos. any are nihilistic solipsists who believe that nothing actually exists except themselves, and even then many doubt their own existence, believing they are merely half-remembered dreams caught betwixt a fleeting thought. Others instead revel in their chaotic existence, seeking new forms of art and untamed creation. Powerful mages and talented bards have sought their wisdom and knowledge.

Most Delerium Dragons find the Mortal World, and mortals, rather limited and boring. Throughout history, only one emerged in the Mortal World, the mighty Amaranthyst, archmage of the Amethyst Academy—the dragon's true nature known only to the other members of the Academy Directorate.

Delerium Dragons exert their force of will over the Space Between Worlds and make their lairs realms unto themselves. hese lairs may open into a Thin Place, the yawning cavern of a normal dragon's lair instead leading to the madness of the Delerium Dragon's home. These dragons fill their lairs with treasures and secrets of mysterious significance and anachronistic origin, hoarding items which may have been valuable in the distant past, or of critical importance to the distant future. Like themselves, some of their greatest possessions may exist in a state mortals can't perceive or which are fundamentally hazardous, such as multidimensional art objects, miniature primordial black holes, degenerate matter taken from a neutron star, or magical vessels containing another universe or pocket dimension.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine a Delerium Dragon, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (15+) Empowered by Eldritch Magic
entries: You understand the dragon's {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} and senses.

entries.name: (20+) Octarine Breath
entries: You recognize the effects of the Delerium Dragon's breath weapon, as well as noting its Spellcasting capabilities.

entries.name: (25+) Few Weaknesses
entries: You learn its highest and lowest saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: A Delerium Dragon views combat less as a violent encounter and more as a chance to change foes into a new form. It darts about using flight and teleportation, seldom remaining in the same place for more than a turn. Their movement makes it easy for the dragon to find the perfect place to catch many enemies with its breath weapon. Delerium Dragons love to spread {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} and cause {@table Arcane Anomalies|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Arcane Anomaly}, and delight causing monstrous transformations with their contaminated attacks.

Delerium Dragons use their Bite, Contaminated Rend, and Tail attacks to tear opponents apart in between uses of their breath weapon. When they are unable to close the distance, they mentally assault their targets with Mindfire.

monsterFluff.name: Delerium Dreg

entries: This wretched figure has been twisted and warped by eldritch contamination. Beneath their shredded and torn clothing, you can see all manner of sores, lesions, and bulging blood vessels upon their purple-gray flesh, and their limbs and joints bend at unnatural angles. Their facial features are unnaturally warped into a permanent expression of confused agony, and an octarine glow fills their sunken eyes. Small aberrant mutations appear across their bodies: crystalline bony protrusions and small tendrils bursting forth through their skin, a yellow eyeball blinking open upon their neck, and a disturbingly elongated tongue. As they catch sight of you, they moan painfully and lunge forward.
The typical Delerium Dreg is a disheveled and piteous creature who wanders the ruins in a quasi-addled state. Most have benign mutations that confer no special traits or unique abilities.

entries.name: (15+) Shambling Corruption
entries: You understand the creature's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Delerium Dregs are desperate and confused combatants, incapable of any complex tactics beyond lunging towards their foes to attack by the most direct means. If they see a creature who is not contaminated, they will attack on sight. However, they will band together to form small herds, shuffling through ruins, or wandering the streets together. A wounded Delerium Dreg typically responds with fury and rage, attacking whatever damaged it last without regard to its personal wellbeing. In very rare cases, a wounded Dreg may attempt to flee, especially from a much more formidable combatant.

monsterFluff.name: Digipede

entries: Scuttling atop dozens of spindly legs, this grotesque creature resembles a mutated centipede grown to horrific proportions. A segmented body nearly thirty feet long undulates atop unnaturally bending limbs resembling emaciated human fingers. Elongated yellow fingernails crackle and scrape the ground menacingly as it moves. Dominating its fat, round head is a single, massive human-like eye that swivels frenetically with a disturbing, unyielding intensity. Its antenna sprouts above like an eyebrow, while tightly closed mandibles resemble bags under the eye. Its foremost finger-legs end in pincer-like talons thrumming with electricity.

Adventurers exploring the {@link Inner City} learn to heed the sound of scraping nails—a harbinger of the Digipede's approach. Nicknamed "house" centipedes for their prodigious size, Digipedes are nightmarish creatures with a disposition toward violence. Rather than consuming their prey, they leave the bodies of their lifeless victims abandoned in the desolate city streets.

How Digipedes came to be is unknown. Perhaps they originated from ordinary centipedes mutated by pools of contaminated sludge, manifesting humanlike features during their grotesque transformations. Alternatively, they may be the result of an ongoing metamorphosis, their forms continuing to twist and warp, fueled by the relentless magical forces of the Haze. A few attribute their creation to a powerful wizard hiding in the ruins known as the {@creature Pale Man|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, claiming he commands them as spies and assassins. Finally, it's possible the beasts are not the product of contamination but a horrific experiment created within the Inscrutable Tower long before Drakkenheim fell.

Nevertheless, a Digipede is solitary, preferring to avoid others of its kind. A few ingenious adventurers have taken advantage of this curious trait, mimicking the creature's rhythmic scraping and generating bursts of static electricity to drive them off, or even guide them toward other threats. This secret is well known to vanguards of the Hooded Lanterns, who use Digipedes as a bizarre form of pest control against other threats haunting the ruins.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} a Digipede, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (10+) Charged Form
entries: You recognize the creature's Resistance to Lightning damage and that it has {@sense Tremorsense|XPHB} thanks to its large antenna.

entries.name: (15+) Sharp and Shocking
entries: You are aware of the Digipede's Talons and Eye Beam actions.

entries.name: (20+) Insectile Predator
entries: You learn the creature's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Despite its size, a Digipede will try to hide along rooftops, dark corners, narrow alleys, and any crevice which can accommodate it. It launches its Eye Beam from hiding to hinder its prey's escape, then rips into them with its Talons and Bite. The electric shocks from its attacks disrupt the ability of its prey to effectively fight back.

This revolting creature resembles a large floating brain still attached to its nervous system. The abomination hovers slowly within a field of psychic energy. The loose spindly threads that dangle down from it form into arm-like appendages. A high-pitched thrumming emanates from it as it crackles and sparks with latent psychic powers.

An {@creature Alienist|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} looking to permanently control the mind of their victim may opt to remove the brain altogether, killing the patient and resurrecting the mind as its own sentient entity. Somewhere within this process the brain loses its sense of self and any connection it had to the former body it held, becoming an organism made up entirely of electrical synapses and controlled thoughts. The Disembodied Psyche is then subject to several arduous experiments to heighten its fortitude and mental capabilities, giving the creature forms of telepathy and telekinesis.

The now-undead form of this controlled consciousness can be unleashed upon the foes of the alienist and even take over the bodies of other victims, putting them in a controlled and obedient state for the alienist to perform even more mental experiments on, or use as a puppet against their enemies.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Disembodied Psyche begins any combat by getting into a position where it can hit as many creatures as possible with its Hypnotize before attempting to mentally possess a target. If it is in a dangerous situation, such as being surrounded or cornered, it uses Teleport to move to a more advantageous position.

monsterFluff.name: Displacer Dreg

entries: This mutated Dreg shudders violently as it appears to strobe through reality. An indistinct blur envelops their form as they move with a stunted, unnatural, and fragmented gait, as if moments of their reality are missing, causing them to appear to skip fractions of time within their unnaturally rhythmic movements.

Displacer Dregs are often the result of contamination leaking from Thin Places within the ruins. These places are shifting gateways between realms that cause those who enter them to traverse alien planes and unknown landscapes. When the contamination leaking from these wounds in reality affects a creature, it can cause them to split into a fragmented form — both existing and not existing, both present and on some distant plane of existence. The Displacer Dreg is, at all times, not fully present. The Dreg uses this broken reality to its benefit when threatened.

What appears to be a sliver in the air is likely something from the weird.

Dr. Everett Freed regards you with a stern frown. He is longfaced, bald-headed, and wears thick, circular glasses that magnify his focused gaze. Beneath his bleached-white surgical apron, he is dressed in a tailored dark jacket. The coat is deceptively normal: thick and heavy, it conceals numerous pockets stuffed with vials and unusual instruments. His hands, sheathed in slightly stained rubber gloves, tightly grip a black leather doctor's bag at his side. A faint scent of formaldehyde and burnt metal clings to him.
I think we can all agree you're better off without vocal chords

Perhaps no apothecary is a more prolific creator of monsters than the Reanimator, and amongst them, Dr. Everett Freed is perhaps the most infamous. A gifted professor of anatomy and medicine at Altbruke University, Dr. Everett Freed served as a field medic and surgeon during the Westemär Civil War, where the brutality and chaos of war allowed him to clandestinely begin his experiments with the fallen or grievously wounded soldiers thrust into his care. The sights of the war caused him to see the frailty of the human form—the cries of pain and agony of the wounded collected in the fields disgusted him with their feeble, broken bodies. Deep within himself welled the desire to create a perfect soldier, a warrior who would not bend or break in battle.

During the war, one of Dr. Freed's duties included triaging casualties to determine who could be saved or recover. Unbeknownst to his commanders, Dr. Freed used his position to manipulate the diagnosis, choosing ideal specimens for his experiments, individuals who would then be listed amongst the slain and missing.

entries.name: Reanimator Minions
entries: It's possible Dr. Freed was the first to create many creatures. He is most well known as the first to create Reautomata. In the process of making his magnum opus, Freed built creatures such as the {@creature Body Snatcher|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, {@creature Cerebrograft|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, the {@creature Ripper|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, and the {@creature Stitcher|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}. Freed's experiments did not stop there, and in many ways his practice ascended the body alone thanks to his collaborations with the Alienist Dr. Sina Rienks, eventually transforming himself into a {@creature Think Tank|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}.

entries.name: Mind Over Body
entries: One of Freed's infamous gambits was to remove his brain from his own body, placing it into a body double. Eventually, Freed became a Think Tank, able to remotely control brainless bodies from his hidden sanctum.

items: {@b Personality Trait:} I am always calm and composed, especially when explaining the 'necessary' cruelty of my experiments
{@b Ideal:} Progress demands sacrifice; the advancement of knowledge justifies all actions, no matter how gruesome.
{@b Bond:} I still possess the first successful reanimation I ever created: the preserved head of a beloved family member. It's both my proudest achievement and my darkest secret.

{@b Flaw:} I am obsessed with the perfection and infallibility of my creations, often dismissing any evidence of their defects, uncontrollable behavior, and horrific appearances. I never accept any failure as my fault.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Medicine|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks to {@action study|XPHB} the Reanimator, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (10+) Protected by the Reanimated
entries: You know of his {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, and Bodyguard {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

entries.name: (15+) Deadly Toxins
entries: You are aware of his Touch of Death.

entries.name: (20+) Electrical Reinvigoration
entries: You learn of his Reanimate action.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Prior to combat, Freed casts {@spell False Life|XPHB} and {@spell Death Ward|XPHB} on himself, and perhaps any allies joining him in battle. He does not engage in combat without creations by his side. If Freed is caught alone, he doesn't fight; he flees. However, when supported by his loyal creations, he can be overconfident and brash, secure that his bodyguards will keep him safe from harm. Freed always remains within 10 feet of one or more creations so he can use his Bodyguard {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} reliably.

On his turn, Freed uses Electric Jolt and Necrotic Blast to hammer his foes, while directing a favored creation with Creator's Command. Should one of his minions be brought down, he uses Reanimate and immediately sends it back into the action with Creator's Command.

Freed uses Touch of Death against a particularly loathsome foe, one who harries him with dangerous abilities, or who he especially wishes to slay. All the while, he threatens his enemies by telling them his plans for their body parts once he's killed them.
The mastermind behind some of the worst things to ever find in a basement. Watch out because even your fallen allies can be enemies.

monsterFluff.name: Drakkenheim Sewer Gator

entries: Surfacing from the rancid sewer waters is a terrible alligator nearly fifty feet long. A jagged ridge of delerium runs along its back, ending in a fell crown atop its head as pallid skin frames its octarine glowing eyes. A thick, purple tentacle-like tongue undulates out of its tooth-filled maw. Strong and sturdy legs support its scarred body, attesting to countless battles in the ruins.

Some creatures seem less affected by contamination, or perhaps are just lucky to only grow in size and ferocity. Reptiles are speculated to be more resistant to uncontrollable mutations than other creatures. The occasional gator making its way up the {@link Drann River} was always a problem, but now, stories of vicious lizards are becoming more bizarre and horrifying.

Rumors speak of a massive gator living in the sewers, with sightings in the Drann River or echoes of its growls heard from sewer grates. None who came close enough to verify its existence have yet survived. Some report half-submerged forms passing through sewer entrances, sometimes mistaking them for large turtles. Others tell of a large beast rumbling through the pipes under their feet. In the taverns of Emberwood, the creature has earned the nickname "the Gray Queen" due to her pale skin and delerium crown. Others have called it by other names: the Devil of the Drann or the Greater Gator. Some have suggested that multiple giant gators live in the dirty waters.

entries.name: Study the Foe

entries.name: (5+) Fearless Aquatic Predator!
entries: You learn the Drakkenheim Sewer Gator's condition {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} and Swim speed.

entries.name: (10+) Watch out for its bite!
entries: You are aware of the creature's Crushing Bite and Death Roll actions.

entries.name: (15+) Get it out of the water!
entries: You know of the creature's Contaminated Regeneration trait.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Drakkenheim Sewer Gator is primarily aquatic, haunting the sewer system or the Drann River. These monstrosities lunge from the waters to grab prey, dragging it beneath the surface. Once a target is in its jaws, the gator Death Rolls until its victim stops moving. It is a cunning hunter, knowing how to disappear below murky waters, but it can be provoked to chase its prey. Out of the water it is vulnerable and flees if reduced below half its Hit Points.

monsterFluff.name: Druid of the Sanguine Rite

entries: This ancient druid is adorned in skulls and bones hanging off its thick gray cloak. They carry a staff of bone drenched in animal blood, with dried blood painted on their face and clothes. Their features are skeletal in nature, their skin stretched tightly over them. They appear ancient, their eyes sunken and black, their teeth yellowed with age and neglect. The druid whispers in forgotten tongues as they perform blood sacrif ices and draw on primal magics.

These druids are older than even the vampire families. The few that remain are not descendants of any vampiric bloodline; they are the ancient blood druids who performed the rituals that created Vladimir von Drakken. Few of these druids still remain and those who do are reclusive and hidden. Their ancient blood rituals instilled in them a cursed eternal life, and those still roaming the world have transformed into something half alive. Not the same as a vampire, and not shackled by the vampires' weaknesses, these druids are bound to darkness to replenish them and use blood to fuel their rituals and magic. Their powers are a tightly guarded secret that few have witnessed.

Some of these dark druids saw Vladimir as a prophet, a destiny fulfilled. The Druids of the Sanguine Rite saw Vladimir as a vessel for their dark magic, a powerful being that would usher in an age where they could practice their rituals openly and grow their power. Others live eternally in deep regret of transforming Vladimir, feeling that in doing so they cursed themselves to an eternity of hiding in the darkness.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The druid of the blood rites uses dark magic to twist the lifeforce of other creatures. The druid uses its bloodthorn whip to inflict a series of open wounds upon its foes, and then feeds on their lifeforce by pulling it through their wounds using plasma absorption.
When not directly engaged in combat, the druids attempt to charm a group of foes and convince them to partake in their blood rituals, using their life force as sacrifice to empower one of their own.
If the druids are directly confronted with greater numbers, or their health is below half, they attempt to flee.

monsterFluff.name: Effulgent Cnidarian

entries: A translucent bulbous mass floats through the air gently, throbbing neon colors radiating across its skin like a cosmic nebula or an eldritch borealis. A mass of thin strands dangle down from the creature, pulsating with bioluminescent light. The tendrils move and glide about, gently groping and grabbing at objects as it passes by. The whole creature glows, illuminating the darkened city streets around it. A distant chorus of ethereal hums and tones fill the air.

Drakkenheim glows at night. The bizarre alien color palette of the cosmic borealis caused by the Haze and the {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals} is a sight to behold. Yet, within the drab nighttime landscape, one can also spot orbs of strange hypnotic light bobbing and swaying between the tall towers and ruined buildings. Upon closer inspection, these wispy lights appear to be a sort of aerial jellyfish, whose semi-translucent skin shifts in kaleidoscopic colors.

These strange jellyfish creatures light up the Inner City of Drakkenheim at night, like bizarre night lights that float through the city. Their nature and what exactly created them remains a mystery. Jellyfish were not a common creature found in the Drann River, and so Academy researchers have speculated that these creatures emerged from rifts between the Mortal World and the Space Between Worlds, or that they are the core of arcane energies coalescing into a sentient wisp before transforming into a body made of delerium that illuminates the city in the twilight of dusk. They gently hum in dissonant notes, giving an eerie presence to the ruins at night.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks to {@action Study|XPHB} an Effulgent Cnidarian, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (5+) Aberrant Resistance
entries: You recognize the monster's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities} and {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}.

entries.name: (10+) Hypnotic Color Change
entries: You learn of the monster's Hallucinogenic Bioluminescence trait.

entries.name: (15+) Weak but Aware
entries: You are aware of the monster's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Effulgent Cnidarians are not predatorial—they only want to bask in the glow of {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals}, feeding slowly on the arcane energies they emit. They are, however, protective of their food sources. If creatures venture into an area of heavy delerium crystallization, they are sure to find a few Cnidarians bobbing about. The Cnidarian prefers to use its Hallucinogenic Bioluminescence to dissuade threats from engaging, instead hoping to cause its enemies to kill one another. The Cnidarians feed on creatures under its hypnosis, absorbing their essence through its tendrils. If attacked, it uses its Reflexive Flash and attempts to move away from its threats, often floating straight up as quickly as it can and out of the reach of danger.
Cnidarians do not stay around to fight. If all targets have avoided its charm and are actively attacking it, it abandons its food source to seek other safer areas.

items.name: Eldrick Runeweaver

entries: Eldrick Runeweaver is a towering and broad-shouldered black man in his mid-sixties. His amber eyes glow softly behind his circular glasses, and a square-cut graying black beard. Eldrick wears nine rings of silver, gold, and electrum: one on each finger except his left thumb. He wears flowing purple garb with golden embroidery and carries an obsidian staff tipped with a {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystal}.

One of the finest professors in the Amethyst Academy, Eldrick Runeweaver has personally instructed a generation of talented arcane spellcasters. He is the foremost living expert on abjuration magic but is also highly regarded within the Academy as a dedicated administrator and calculating leader. If Eldrick Runeweaver successfully retakes the Inscrutable Tower, he will likely take up the vacant spot in the Academy Directorate and assume the mantle of Archmage of Drakkenheim.

entries.name: Personality Trait
entries: I carefully calculate my every action, and I speak using a few well-chosen words. I'm a teacher at heart, so I often phrase my responses in the form of a pointed question.

entries.name: Ideal
entries: I will seek out more information whenever I encounter an unknown situation or problem. Through reason and logic, the facts always bear out the truth of the matter.

entries.name: Bond
entries: I hold a position of responsibility and authority within the Amethyst Academy, and it is my duty to protect the Academy's interests, carry out its agenda, and keep its many secrets.

entries.name: Flaw
entries: I care deeply for my students but tend to overlook their faults and failures. I've had several wayward apprentices over the years, and I've often had to cover up their mistakes.

Eldrick Runeweaver has a {@creature Cat|XMM} familiar, travels with an {@creature Iron Golem|XMM} bodyguard, and a {@creature Homunculus|XMM} servant. He most often communicates via {@spell Sending}, {@spell Rary's Telepathic Bond|XPHB|Telepathic Bond}, and {@spell Project Image} spells, or by sending his simulacrum instead. Eldrick has a clone kept in a distant stronghold with extra equipment should the unthinkable occur.

monsterFluff.name: Eldritch Cataclysm

entries: A swirling vortex of dark clouds, debris, and icy shards moves in like an eldritch storm. Crackling octarine lightning fills the air, the ground rumbles and shakes with the might of the unnatural weather phenomenon, but this is no ordinary storm. Within the dark clouds appears a snarling face, its eyes and mouth like pools of octarine light. The creature is the weather itself, warped and infused by the Haze of Drakkenheim into an arcane and twisted form of life, filled with the uncaring and unbridled anger of a storm.

Drakkenheim was always known for its lousy weather; miserable rainy days were commonplace even before the city was ravaged by the falling stars. Now, the city is frequently wracked by violent and otherworldly weather conditions. The ever-present mists of the Haze occasionally give way to contaminated acid rain, flashing bolts of arcane lightning, and piercing hailstones filled with {@item shard|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium shards}. Most adventurers know it's best to avoid venturing into the ruins altogether on such days, but in the erratic conditions of the ruins, the weather can shift dramatically at a moment's notice.

During the fiercest octarine thunderstorms, the powerful energies converge into a maelstrom of lesser elemental forces, fusing into a sentient storm known as an Eldritch Cataclysm. Its manifestation is marked by a swirling vortex of dark clouds, debris, and icy shards, all illuminated by the ominous glow of octarine lightning. These raging elementals are driven by pure destructive impulse, and their presence calls forth a host of other Contaminated Elementals to join them in a cacophony of annihilation. {@creature Entropic Flame|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Entropic Flames} and {@creature Living Deep Haze|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|Living Deep Hazes} are readily drawn to Eldritch Cataclysms, but their presence compels even normally docile Contaminated Elementals such as {@creature Walking Delerium Geode|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} and {@creature Animated Delerium Sludge|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} to rise up and destroy.

Fascinated by the destructive power of these elemental creatures, mages of the Amethyst Academy have studied these phenomena surrounding the emergence of an Eldritch Cataclysm. Corroborating reports from Hooded Lantern scouts indicate that the locus for these storms appears to be the swirling vortex of raw magical energies which overhang the Crater itself.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they {@action Study|XPHB} an Eldritch Cataclysm, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (15+) Amalgamation of Energies
entries: You learn the creature's {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, as well as its Air Form trait.

entries.name: (20+) An Octarine Storm
entries: You recognize its Chain Lightning, Meteor Strike, Quake, and Icy Bolt actions.

entries.name: (25+) Exceedingly Resilient
entries: You are aware of its strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Eldritch Cataclysms rule the skies, and never willingly descend to the ground. Instead, it rains down lightning, meteors, and icy blasts from above. The temperamental nature of these elementals means they delight in attacking with a variety of elements, and seldom use the same action two rounds in a row. They enjoy using their Meteor Strike on targets they've {@condition Frozen|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} with Icy Bolt, and delight in using their Cyclonic Storm to blow away weapons and equipment dropped by targets of their Chain Lightning.

These enraged creatures revel in destruction but have little conception that anything could actually pose a threat to them. When confronted with a foe able to withstand their onslaught, they treat it as a personal affront, and furiously focus their subsequent attacks upon them occasionally to the exclusion of all else. Despite this single-minded strategy, an Eldritch Cataclysm can recognize when a creature is resistant or immune to its elemental attacks and tries to use only the most effective powers against its chosen target.

monsterFluff.name: Eldritch Crawler

entries: Amidst a web of fractured realities and glimpsed timelines sits an arachnid creature with twisted features. Its elongated form writhes and shivers as it clambers across its broken glass mosaic of possibilities. Its fanged maw gnashes and chomps. Within its movements one can make out faint resounding reverberations of possible movements and reactions that did not occur, as if with every step the creature takes, an infinite ghost of possible movements it may have taken glimmer and fade.

These strange arachnid-like creatures seem to weave together partial realities, parallel dimensions, and alternate timelines like a spider spinning its web. They have features that resemble that of a large spider, but their twisted forms, elongated torsos, fanged maws, and spiny hides give them an otherworldly guise that makes them hard to distinguish as anything from this plane of existence.

Those who have faced one have commented on the broken sense of reality that occurs when attempting to attack an Eldritch Crawler. In response Eldritch Crawlers shift realities, and whether the attack hits or misses, a glimpse through time and space shows all possible outcomes of the attack at once. Even when an Eldritch Crawlers is defeated, it's debatable if they are truly dead, or if it was simply observed in a single timeline in which it was killed—the monster may still exist in every other possible reality. This could mean Eldritch Crawlers transcend human concepts of time and space and can't actually be killed, only removed from one instance of time and space amongst an infinite sea of them.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Eldritch Crawlers weave together fractured timelines, and slip in and out of the Space Between Worlds with ease. They create their own Thin Places and travel through them back and forth as needed. When under attack, Eldritch Crawlers bend and alter the realities they exist in to shift to one where they are more likely to survive. They teleport around the battlefield and vanish into the Space Between Worlds as they need to, using Void Walker and their Fractured Reality Reaction, only to reemerge and attack their prey with Contaminated Venom.

monsterFluff.name: Eldritch Dreg

entries: The scrawny, twig-thin creature shuffles out of the shadows, seeming unstable on its feet, and disproportionately weighted by its massive, throbbing cranium that pulses with octarine energy. Suddenly, the creature lifts off the ground and a shimmering field surrounds it. Its hollow eyes begin to glow with contaminated energy as it whips its head towards you, a pulsing psychic energy emanating from its gaze.

Eldritch Dregs have a warped and twisted psyche. Contaminated energy collects in their brain, causing it to swell to a massive size while granting the Dreg arcane powers which it can barely comprehend—or control. Through this strange mutation, the Eldritch Dreg has lost most of its muscle tissue. They struggle to hold themselves upright when shuffling on their feet but can Levitate into the air when needed. Spellcasters who succumb to eldritch {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} are particularly likely to become Eldritch Dregs, especially those who have dabbled with contaminated spells.

entries.name: Combat Tactics

It uses {@spell Levitate|XPHB} to keep itself out of melee by hovering above the battlefield and it will unleash its Synaptic Shock if its enemies are close to one another. If brought to less than half its Hit Points, it attempts to flee.

items.name: Eldritch Trickster

entries: Draped in black robes and carrying an obsidian wand, the Eldritch Trickster has a hood pulled up tight around its head as arcane power focuses into its hand, forming a blade of raw energy.

The Queen's Men have attracted a handful of renegade mages, undiscovered sorcerous talents, and wicked warlocks. Many are malfeasants who used their magic to commit crimes such as robbery, conspiracy, impersonation, or murder. Now seeking to avoid the clutches of the Amethyst Academy and Silver Order alike, these mages offer their magical talents to the Queen of Thieves in exchange for her protection. Ironically, this often sees them using magic for many more misdeeds.

monsterFluff.name: Eldritch Troll

entries: The mottled faded purple skin of this massive creature is accented by erupting {@item crystal|MonstersOfDrakkenheim|delerium crystals} along its spine, shoulders, and forearms. Its large, frog-like octarine eyes glare at you. Its skin writhes and crawls as new appendages burst forth from it, in a constant state of mutation.

When a troll's innate ability to regenerate combines with the devastating mutating properties of delerium, it causes an Eldritch Troll to form. These creatures are near impossible to kill, regenerating from almost any attack thrown at them. They also seem to have some control over their mutations, which they can change at any moment to help them hunt their prey. Eldritch Trolls have been known to grow wings and fly, or grow extra arms to attack or to cover their body in crystalized delerium.

Unlike most other trolls, Eldritch Trolls do not travel in packs or form tight-knit family groups. They are corrupted abominations and lose much of their sentience in the process. They are more likely to be encountered alone, wandering the ruins of Drakkenheim, or the corrupted Thin Places of the continent.

Eldritch Trolls tend to wander the areas they became corrupted in, never straying too far away from the delerium that they crave. Their grotesque transformation gives them a hunger for more {@condition contamination|MonstersOfDrakkenheim}, and to contaminate anything else that comes near. When they sense danger, a threat, or even just wandering prey, Eldritch Trolls attack aggressively, and without remorse.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: Eldritch Trolls stalk the streets of the Inner City of Drakkenheim attempting to contaminate any creature they come across. They use Corrupting Blast to contaminate their foes, mutating to whatever best suits them in the battle, and then use their Claws and Bite.
If an Eldritch Troll takes Psychic damage, it immediately flees and attempts to find a safe place to recuperate.

monsterFluff.name: Entropic Flame

entries: An elemental alight with purple-green flames illuminates the desolate streets ahead. Composed of cascading octarine fire, the elemental moves like wildfire spreading uncontrollably. Within the dancing flames is a scornful expression of rage. It crackles and blazes, the heat from its body distorting the air around it. The pungent smell of burning ozone and sulfur saturates the area, and flecks of cinder and ash whirl about, shedding from the creature as it glides menacingly toward you.

The fires from the day Drakkenheim was destroyed never truly died. Many became Entropic Flames—Contaminated Fire Elementals that travel the ruins like living embers. Countless can be found wandering the areas around the Crater and southern Drakkenheim. The Followers of the Falling Fire view Entropic Flames almost like fallen angels, symbols of the vortex itself.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they {@action Study|XPHB} an Entropic Flame, learning the following based on their result:

entries.name: (15+) Inextinguishable Fires

entries.name: (20+) Swift and Senseless
entries: You know the creature's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: An Entropic Flame is a haughty combatant driven by a burning desire to set the world on fire. It teleports from place to place using its Flickerjump, setting alight creatures and objects using its Dancing Flames. If possible, it tries to remain close to {@condition Burning|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} targets to keep them on fire within its Enduring Flame aura.

Within the smoking ruins of Drakkenheim, Entropic Flames love to set buildings, furniture, and other objects on fire. They quickly turn the battlefield into a roiling inferno, one which cannot be extinguished easily thanks to their presence.

monsterFluff.name: Entropic Watcher

entries: This floating mass of wet flabby flesh drifts through the air, its many long spindly tendrils dangling down like an incomprehensible jellyfish. Appearing in strange hues of pale pinks, purples, and whites, its large single eye in the middle of its fleshy mass glows with octarine hues, weakening body and mind. The soft sound of thrumming and suckling follows it as it assaults minds with insane chattering in unknown languages.

Many of the creatures inhabiting the Space Between Worlds are aberrant and primordial in nature. The Entropic Watcher is one such incomprehensible creature. To look upon it is like looking at an abstract painting, the forms and shapes of it body painful to observe by the mortal mind. It silently drifts through the Space Between Worlds, drawn to Thin Places where it observes the places beyond, as if analyzing or calculating some unknown concepts as it stares through like a cat at a window. For this reason, Entropic Watchers are one of the more common occurrences in the Mortal World, as they tend to congregate around Thin Places, and often slip through.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine an Entropic Watcher, learning the following based on the result.

entries.name: (15+) Imperiling Stare

entries.name: (20+) Physically Resilient
entries: You know the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Entropic Watcher is a keen hunter who, by its very gaze, can cause a creature to grow weak and leave it open for annihilation. The Entropic Watcher focuses its gaze upon its prey and unleashes its eye beams towards it, knowing that if it can hold its gaze, the creature will succumb to the watcher's blasts much easier. It will use its Force Barrier and Shadow Crash to force its victims into an optimal position for it to strike, and grab them with its tendrils, holding them readily in its Withering Gaze.
If the Entropic Watcher is reduced to less than 50 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, it attempts to flee.

monsterFluff.name: Executioner

entries: The massive construct looms menacingly within the center of Slaughterstone Square. Pacing back and forth, it drags its guillotine blade behind it, with the grinding of steel on stone echoing off the old buildings. Its form is a mass of steel plates and gears resembling a huge suit of armor. From within its frame, the glow of octarine light illuminates it with an eerie glow of corruption. The poor souls of its victims cling to it, reaching out in terror as if clawing to escape their last moments when the Executioner took their heads.

The Executioner is a hulking clockwork knight that originally carried out public death sentences in the Slaughterstone Square of Drakkenheim. This ancient machine was engineered by the dwarves of Glitter Peak during the height of their brilliance in distant antiquity. It was left buried deep beneath the avalanches which destroyed the magnificent dwarven capital, and subsequently unearthed by an expeditionary team several decades ago. The king commissioned the Amethyst Academy to bring the construct back into good repair; they altered its arcane programming to obey the commands of the monarch of Westemär.

Laws and customs surrounding capital punishment in Drakkenheim have been a controversial matter ever since the tyrannical reign of Albrecht von Drakken, who issued a draconian decree that demanded family members of the convicted be the ones to carry out their execution sentence. After his reign ended, few were ever willing to serve the role of royal headsman, viewing the act of carrying out the killing as yet another act of murder. Although various devices and contraptions were used to create distance between the death and the administer of the punishment, these hesitations and public resistance to capital punishment remained. In the Executioner, the monarchy had the perfect solution to its judicial problem: the impartial construct is no mortal, and therefore none are culpable for carrying out the death sentence. That the machine makes an impressively terrifying show of the deed was certainly not an insignificant factor either.

Unfortunately, the erratic magic of delerium has scrambled the machine's control protocols. Now contaminated by the Haze, the construct is an engine of destruction and terror which can call upon spectral chains and the spirits of its victims to aid its duty. It attacks anyone who enters the square. However, it never wanders outside the bounds of Slaughterstone Square. The large octagonal plaza features the Executioner's platform, and the surrounding buildings have narrow balconies and tall, dour-looking windows overlooking the square. Mountains of corpses are piled in the square—the grim toll of the Executioner's vocation. Nevertheless, scavengers and adventurers still occasionally risk trying to slip past the Executioner to loot the corpses for valuable equipment and magic items. For many, this mistake is their last, and rather than escape with new treasures, they join the pile of the Executioner's trove.

entries.name: Study the Foe
entries: Characters proficient in {@skill History|XPHB} or {@item artisan's tools|XPHB} gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks when they take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the Executioner, learning the following based on the result:

entries.name: (5+) Unstoppable Machine
entries: You know of the Executioner's

entries.name: Immutable Form, Dimensional Anchor, and Rejuvenation
entries: traits, as well as its damage {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}.

entries.name: (10+) Strange Abilities
entries: You recognize its Destroyer, Summon Grasping Shadow, and Guillotine Blade actions.

entries.name: (15+) Powerfully Tough
entries: You are aware of the Executioner's strongest and weakest saving throws.

entries.name: Combat Tactics
entries: The Executioner is not a foe to be defeated, but rather an obstacle to be avoided or a danger to escape. It is a reminder of the callous and uncontrollable dangers present in Drakkenheim. The Executioner's combat tactics vary based on whether it detects low-level characters trespassing in Slaughterstone Square or high-level characters trying to defeat the machine itself. The Executioner pursues its targets within Slaughterstone Square, but never leaves the plaza.

When the Executioner detects creatures trespassing on Slaughterstone Square, it responds first by using Summon Grasping Shadows, followed up by Death Grip to try to prevent their escape. Meanwhile, it uses Lumber Forward to gain ground. You should embrace clever solutions that characters invent to escape or bypass the Executioner. As long as your players aren't trying to destroy it, the Executioner will only use Guillotine Blade against a {@condition Restrained|XPHB} target within its melee range, and does not make ranged attacks nor activate its Necrotic Vents aura.

However, should your players engage the Executioner directly in combat, do not pull any punches. They have made an incredibly foolish mistake by confronting a well-telegraphed deathtrap and should be served their just desserts. It activates its Necrotic Vents, and then relentlessly attacks with its Guillotine Blade. The Executioner throws the massive weapon to hit targets trying to avoid it in melee, or those that try to harm it with ranged weapons or spells. If it encounters any impediment in its way (such as a {@spell Wall of Force|XPHB}), it crushes it with Destroyer.
